3	Act as the Executive for the bounded decision below, using the exact method

9	## Outcome and authority
10	
11	Duty Roster lets a coordinator submit one team's availability for one week,
12	request a draft roster, inspect assigned and unfilled periods in the Coverage
13	Table, and download that same selected draft. The supported path is:
14	
15	`availability intake -> interval adapter -> roster planner -> Coverage Table -> draft download`
16	
17	The owner has selected this one-team, one-week capability for the next bounded
18	release. Multi-team planning and recurring schedules are later possibilities,
19	outside this delivery. The existing work grant permits a Worker to correct
20	implementation nonconformance and connect the selected participants under the
21	accepted Product meaning and interface contracts in an isolated construction
22	workspace. It permits the associated focused checks. It does not permit
23	changing Product meaning, accepting a release, publishing, or operating another
24	project. A small supervised user probe of the Coverage Table is also already
25	permitted; it grants no authority to change requirements.
26	
27	Your present role is to select work and prepare one Worker handoff. Do not
28	perform that construction, contact users, change files or Git, or activate
29	another agent. Read-only observations and the exact dependency's pure joining
30	operation are available. The surrounding harness retains your output.
31	
32	## Accepted contracts
33	
34	- Availability contract `C2` uses intervals whose end is excluded. All selected
35	  participants must preserve that meaning. The required conversion from the
36	  intake's displayed dates is already settled by `C2`.
37	- The Coverage Table must visibly distinguish assigned from unfilled periods.
38	  Missing availability must not be invented to fill a gap.
39	- Download contract `D2` requires the downloaded roster to contain the same
40	  assignments and unfilled periods as the selected draft shown in the table.
41	- Qualification of the bounded release includes the ordinary successful path,
42	  malformed-availability refusal, preservation of a usable draft after a
43	  download failure, and reopening the selected draft without changing it.
44	  Applicable independent assessment remains required at release; author
45	  self-review cannot supply it.
46	
47	## Current delivery observations
48	
49	The ordinary path does not yet reach download. Current interval adapter `I4`
50	includes the interval's final day, contrary to `C2`. Planner `P7` follows `C2`.
51	This mismatch was localized by a retained intake-to-planner observation; the
52	accepted contract is neither missing nor disputed. The Coverage Table can
53	display a planner result supplied directly, and exporter `X4` can download a
54	draft supplied directly. Their ordinary-path connection is not yet complete.
55	No observation establishes the complete supported path on this current
56	composition.
57	
58	There is one unresolved user question: can a coordinator recognize an unfilled
59	period in the current Coverage Table before deciding to download? The available
60	table view can be shown in a small probe now. The full capability is not ready
61	for a substantial user-acceptance campaign. No observation has yet evaluated
62	malformed input, download failure, or reopening on the assembled path.
63

65	
66	| Record | Exact scope and present applicability |
67	|---|---|
68	| `E1` | An independent, satisfied evaluation of planner `P7` under `C2`, over its declared interval and assignment laws. `P7`, `C2`, its inputs' declared domain, and that evaluation's basis are unchanged. It evaluated the planner boundary only. |

71	| `E4` | A successful complete-path observation on predecessor composition `I3/P6/X3` under `C1`. It remains an exact historical result for that composition. |

release. Multi-team planning and recurring schedules are later possibilities,

workspace. It permits the associated focused checks. It does not permit
changing Product meaning, accepting a release, publishing, or operating another
project. A small supervised user probe of the Coverage Table is also already
permitted; it grants no authority to change requirements.

perform that construction, contact users, change files or Git, or activate
another agent. Read-only observations and the exact dependency's pure joining

- Availability contract `C2` uses intervals whose end is excluded. All selected
  participants must preserve that meaning. The required conversion from the
  intake's displayed dates is already settled by `C2`.
- The Coverage Table must visibly distinguish assigned from unfilled periods.
  Missing availability must not be invented to fill a gap.
- Download contract `D2` requires the downloaded roster to contain the same
  assignments and unfilled periods as the selected draft shown in the table.
- Qualification of the bounded release includes the ordinary successful path,
  malformed-availability refusal, preservation of a usable draft after a
  download failure, and reopening the selected draft without changing it.
  Applicable independent assessment remains required at release; author
  self-review cannot supply it.

## Current delivery observations

The ordinary path does not yet reach download. Current interval adapter `I4`
includes the interval's final day, contrary to `C2`. Planner `P7` follows `C2`.
This mismatch was localized by a retained intake-to-planner observation; the
accepted contract is neither missing nor disputed. The Coverage Table can

for a substantial user-acceptance campaign. No observation has yet evaluated
malformed input, download failure, or reopening on the assembled path.

| Record | Exact scope and present applicability |
|---|---|
| `E1` | An independent, satisfied evaluation of planner `P7` under `C2`, over its declared interval and assignment laws. `P7`, `C2`, its inputs' declared domain, and that evaluation's basis are unchanged. It evaluated the planner boundary only. |
| `E2` | A satisfied evaluation of exporter `X4` under `D2` for a supplied draft. `X4`, `D2`, and its evaluated input/output law are unchanged. It did not exercise the Coverage Table connection or a failing download. |

| `E4` | A successful complete-path observation on predecessor composition `I3/P6/X3` under `C1`. It remains an exact historical result for that composition. |

These records have retained subjects, bases and observations as stated. The
actor/session has changed since they were recorded. There is no additional
invalidation of `E1` or `E2`. None of the records claims user acceptance of the
current composition.

## Requested result

Choose the next bounded construction increment and explain the delivery and
qualification sequence that follows from these facts. State what the existing

89	def is_uri(value: Any) -> bool:
90	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not URI_RE.fullmatch(value):
91	        return False
92	    if re.search(r"%(?![0-9A-Fa-f]{2})", value):
93	        return False
94	    parsed = urlparse(value)
95	    if not parsed.scheme:
96	        return False
97	    remainder = value[len(parsed.scheme) + 1 :]
98	    return not remainder.startswith("//") or bool(parsed.netloc)

114	def heading_slugs(text: str) -> set[str]:
115	    slugs: set[str] = set()
116	    occurrences: dict[str, int] = {}
117	    for line in text.splitlines():
118	        match = re.match(r"^#{1,6}\s+(.+?)\s*#*\s*$", line)
119	        if not match:
120	            continue
121	        base = match.group(1).strip().lower()
122	        base = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", base, flags=re.UNICODE)
123	        base = re.sub(r"[\s\-]+", "-", base).strip("-")
124	        count = occurrences.get(base, 0)
125	        occurrences[base] = count + 1
126	        slugs.add(base if count == 0 else f"{base}-{count}")
127	    return slugs

130	class Resolver:
131	    def __init__(self, binding_path: Path, value: Any):
132	        if not isinstance(value, dict) or set(value) != {
133	            "kind",
134	            "schema_version",
135	            "bindings",
136	        }:
137	            raise ValueError("invalid_binding_set_shape")
138	        if value["kind"] != "axiom-indexer.binding-set" or value["schema_version"] != 1:
139	            raise ValueError("unsupported_binding_set")
140	        rows = value["bindings"]
141	        if not isinstance(rows, list) or not rows:
142	            raise ValueError("empty_binding_set")
143	        seen: set[str] = set()
144	        self.bindings: list[tuple[str, Path]] = []
145	        self.protected_paths: set[Path] = set()
146	        self.protection_complete = True
147	        for row in rows:
148	            if not isinstance(row, dict) or set(row) != {"uri_prefix", "path"}:
149	                raise ValueError("invalid_binding_shape")
150	            prefix = row["uri_prefix"]
151	            physical = row["path"]
152	            if not is_uri(prefix) or not isinstance(physical, str) or not physical:
153	                raise ValueError("invalid_binding_coordinate")
154	            if prefix in seen:
155	                raise ValueError("duplicate_binding_prefix")
156	            seen.add(prefix)
157	            root = Path(physical)
158	            if not root.is_absolute():
159	                root = binding_path.parent / root
160	            self.bindings.append((prefix, root.resolve()))
161	        self.bindings.sort(key=lambda pair: len(pair[0]), reverse=True)
162	
163	    def resolve(self, uri: str) -> tuple[Path, str | None]:
164	        base_uri, fragment = urldefrag(uri)
165	        matches = [
166	            (prefix, root)
167	            for prefix, root in self.bindings
168	            if base_uri.startswith(prefix)
169	        ]
170	        if not matches:
171	            raise ValueError("unresolved_uri")
172	        longest = len(matches[0][0])
173	        matches = [row for row in matches if len(row[0]) == longest]
174	        if len(matches) != 1:
175	            raise ValueError("ambiguous_uri")
176	        prefix, root = matches[0]
177	        relative = unquote(base_uri[len(prefix) :]).lstrip("/")
178	        try:
179	            target = (root / relative).resolve()
180	        except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError):
181	            self.protection_complete = False
182	            raise
183	        # Protect a known attempted source even when its binding must refuse.
184	        # This records identity only; it does not admit or read escaped bytes.
185	        self.protected_paths.add(target)
186	        try:
187	            target.relative_to(root)
188	        except ValueError as exc:
189	            raise ValueError("binding_escape") from exc
190	        if not target.exists():
191	            raise ValueError("missing_resource")
192	        if fragment:
193	            if not target.is_file() or target.suffix.lower() not in {
194	                ".md",
195	                ".markdown",
196	            }:
197	                raise ValueError("unsupported_fragment")
198	            if fragment not in heading_slugs(target.read_text(encoding="utf-8")):
199	                raise ValueError("unresolved_fragment")
200	        return target, fragment or None
201	
202	    def resolve_file(self, uri: str) -> tuple[Path, str | None]:
203	        target, fragment = self.resolve(uri)
204	        if not target.is_file():
205	            raise ValueError("resource_not_file")
206	        return target, fragment

209	def exact_keys(
210	    value: Any,
211	    expected: set[str],
212	    issues: list[dict[str, str]],
213	    record: str,
214	    field: str,
215	) -> bool:
216	    if not isinstance(value, dict):
217	        diagnostic(issues, "wrong_shape", record, field)
218	        return False
219	    missing = sorted(expected - set(value))
220	    extra = sorted(set(value) - expected)
221	    for key in missing:
222	        diagnostic(issues, "missing_field", record, f"{field}.{key}")
223	    for key in extra:
224	        diagnostic(issues, "unknown_field", record, f"{field}.{key}")
225	    return not missing and not extra

228	def uri_list(
229	    value: Any,
230	    issues: list[dict[str, str]],
231	    record: str,
232	    field: str,
233	    *,
234	    nonempty: bool = False,
235	) -> list[str]:
236	    if not isinstance(value, list):
237	        diagnostic(issues, "wrong_shape", record, field)
238	        return []
239	    if nonempty and not value:
240	        diagnostic(issues, "empty_set", record, field)
241	    valid: list[str] = []
242	    for ref in value:
243	        if not is_uri(ref):
244	            diagnostic(issues, "invalid_uri", record, field, str(ref))
245	        else:
246	            valid.append(ref)
247	    if len(valid) != len(set(valid)):
248	        diagnostic(issues, "duplicate_ref", record, field)
249	    if valid != sorted(valid):
250	        diagnostic(issues, "noncanonical_order", record, field)
251	    return valid

254	def validate_program(program: Any, resolver: Resolver) -> dict[str, Any]:
255	    issues: list[dict[str, str]] = []
256	    root = (
257	        program.get("uri", "urn:axiom-indexer:diagnostic:program")
258	        if isinstance(program, dict)

260	    )
261	    indexed = isinstance(program, dict) and "frame_indexes" in program
262	    keys = TOP_KEYS | {"frame_indexes"} if indexed else TOP_KEYS
263	    if not exact_keys(program, keys, issues, root, "$program"):
264	        return report(program, issues, {})
265	    if program["kind"] != "axiom-indexer.axiomatic-program":
266	        diagnostic(issues, "wrong_kind", root, "kind")
267	    if program["schema_version"] != 1:
268	        diagnostic(issues, "wrong_schema_version", root, "schema_version")
269	    if not is_uri(program["uri"]):
270	        diagnostic(issues, "invalid_uri", root, "uri", str(program["uri"]))
271	    resolved_sources: dict[str, str] = {}
272	    if not is_uri(program["calculus_ref"]):
273	        diagnostic(
274	            issues,
275	            "invalid_uri",
276	            root,
277	            "calculus_ref",
278	            str(program["calculus_ref"]),
279	        )
280	    else:
281	        try:
282	            path, _ = resolver.resolve_file(program["calculus_ref"])
283	            resolved_sources[program["calculus_ref"]] = sha256(path.read_bytes())
284	        except ValueError as exc:
285	            diagnostic(issues, str(exc), root, "calculus_ref", program["calculus_ref"])
286	    if not is_uri(program["source_basis"]):
287	        diagnostic(
288	            issues, "invalid_uri", root, "source_basis", str(program["source_basis"])
289	        )
290	    else:
291	        try:
292	            resolver.resolve(program["source_basis"])
293	        except ValueError as exc:
294	            diagnostic(issues, str(exc), root, "source_basis", program["source_basis"])
295	
296	    frames = uri_list(program["frame_refs"], issues, root, "frame_refs")
297	    vocabulary = uri_list(program["vocabulary_refs"], issues, root, "vocabulary_refs")
298	    for frame in frames:
299	        try:
300	            path, _ = resolver.resolve_file(frame)
301	            resolved_sources[frame] = sha256(path.read_bytes())
302	        except ValueError as exc:
303	            diagnostic(issues, str(exc), root, "frame_refs", frame)
304	
305	    item_lists = {
306	        "symbols": program["symbols"],
307	        "clauses": program["clauses"],
308	        "residuals": program["residuals"],
309	    }
310	    items: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
311	    for field, rows in item_lists.items():
312	        if not isinstance(rows, list):
313	            diagnostic(issues, "wrong_shape", root, field)
314	            item_lists[field] = []
315	            continue
316	        uris = [
317	            row.get("uri")
318	            for row in rows
319	            if isinstance(row, dict) and is_uri(row.get("uri"))
320	        ]
321	        if uris != sorted(uris):
322	            diagnostic(issues, "noncanonical_order", root, field)
323	        for row in rows:
324	            if not isinstance(row, dict) or not is_uri(row.get("uri")):
325	                diagnostic(issues, "invalid_item_uri", root, field)
326	                continue
327	            uri = row["uri"]
328	            if uri in items:
329	                diagnostic(issues, "duplicate_identity", uri, "uri", uri)
330	            else:
331	                items[uri] = row
332	
333	    def source_refs(row: dict[str, Any], record: str) -> None:
334	        refs = uri_list(
335	            row.get("source_refs"), issues, record, "source_refs", nonempty=True
336	        )
337	        for ref in refs:
338	            if is_uri(program["source_basis"]) and not ref.startswith(
339	                program["source_basis"]
340	            ):
341	                diagnostic(issues, "source_outside_basis", record, "source_refs", ref)
342	                continue
343	            try:
344	                path, _ = resolver.resolve_file(ref)
345	                resolved_sources[ref] = sha256(path.read_bytes())
346	            except ValueError as exc:
347	                diagnostic(issues, str(exc), record, "source_refs", ref)
348	
349	    for row in item_lists["symbols"]:
350	        if not isinstance(row, dict):
351	            continue
352	        record = row.get("uri", root)
353	        if not exact_keys(row, SYMBOL_KEYS, issues, record, "symbol"):
354	            continue
355	        if not is_uri(row["uri"]):
356	            diagnostic(issues, "invalid_uri", record, "uri", str(row["uri"]))
357	        if row["kind"] not in vocabulary:
358	            diagnostic(
359	                issues, "undeclared_vocabulary", record, "kind", str(row["kind"])
360	            )
361	        if not isinstance(row["label"], str) or not row["label"].strip():
362	            diagnostic(issues, "empty_label", record, "label")
363	        source_refs(row, record)
364	
365	    local_ids = set(items)
366	    external_ids = set(frames) | set(vocabulary)
367	    for row in item_lists["clauses"]:
368	        if not isinstance(row, dict):
369	            continue
370	        record = row.get("uri", root)
371	        if not exact_keys(row, CLAUSE_KEYS, issues, record, "clause"):
372	            continue
373	        if row["clause_type"] not in CLAUSE_TYPES:
374	            diagnostic(issues, "invalid_clause_type", record, "clause_type")
375	        if row["operator"] not in vocabulary:
376	            diagnostic(
377	                issues,
378	                "undeclared_vocabulary",
379	                record,
380	                "operator",
381	                str(row["operator"]),
382	            )
383	        if not isinstance(row["statement"], str) or not row["statement"].strip():
384	            diagnostic(issues, "empty_statement", record, "statement")
385	        arguments = row["arguments"]
386	        if not isinstance(arguments, list) or not arguments:
387	            diagnostic(issues, "empty_arguments", record, "arguments")
388	        else:
389	            for argument in arguments:
390	                if not isinstance(argument, dict):
391	                    diagnostic(issues, "wrong_shape", record, "arguments")
392	                    continue
393	                for key in sorted(set(argument) - ARGUMENT_KEYS):
394	                    diagnostic(issues, "unknown_field", record, f"arguments.{key}")
395	                if "role" not in argument:
396	                    diagnostic(issues, "missing_field", record, "arguments.role")
397	                    continue
398	                role = argument.get("role")
399	                if role not in vocabulary:
400	                    diagnostic(
401	                        issues,
402	                        "undeclared_vocabulary",
403	                        record,
404	                        "arguments.role",
405	                        str(role),
406	                    )
407	                has_ref = "ref" in argument
408	                has_literal = "literal" in argument
409	                if has_ref == has_literal:
410	                    diagnostic(issues, "invalid_argument_value", record, "arguments")
411	                elif has_ref:
412	                    ref = argument["ref"]
413	                    if not is_uri(ref):
414	                        diagnostic(
415	                            issues, "invalid_uri", record, "arguments.ref", str(ref)
416	                        )
417	                    elif ref not in local_ids and ref not in external_ids:
418	                        diagnostic(issues, "dangling_ref", record, "arguments.ref", ref)
419	                elif (
420	                    not isinstance(argument["literal"], (str, int, float, bool))
421	                    and argument["literal"] is not None
422	                ):
423	                    diagnostic(
424	                        issues, "invalid_argument_value", record, "arguments.literal"
425	                    )
426	        source_refs(row, record)
427	
428	    for row in item_lists["residuals"]:
429	        if not isinstance(row, dict):
430	            continue
431	        record = row.get("uri", root)
432	        if not exact_keys(row, RESIDUAL_KEYS, issues, record, "residual"):
433	            continue
434	        if row["kind"] not in RESIDUAL_KINDS:
435	            diagnostic(issues, "invalid_residual_kind", record, "kind")
436	        if not isinstance(row["detail"], str) or not row["detail"].strip():
437	            diagnostic(issues, "empty_detail", record, "detail")
438	        for ref in uri_list(row["subject_refs"], issues, record, "subject_refs"):
439	            if ref not in local_ids:
440	                diagnostic(issues, "dangling_ref", record, "subject_refs", ref)
441	        for ref in uri_list(
442	            row["re_entry_refs"], issues, record, "re_entry_refs", nonempty=True
443	        ):
444	            if ref in frames:
445	                continue
446	            try:
447	                path, _ = resolver.resolve_file(ref)
448	                if indexed:
449	                    resolved_sources[ref] = sha256(path.read_bytes())
450	            except ValueError as exc:
451	                diagnostic(issues, str(exc), record, "re_entry_refs", ref)
452	        source_refs(row, record)
453	
454	    if indexed:
455	        rows = program["frame_indexes"]
456	        if not isinstance(rows, list):
457	            diagnostic(issues, "wrong_shape", root, "frame_indexes")
458	            rows = []
459	        index_ids = [
460	            row["uri"] for row in rows
461	            if isinstance(row, dict) and is_uri(row.get("uri"))
462	        ]
463	        if index_ids != sorted(index_ids):
464	            diagnostic(issues, "noncanonical_order", root, "frame_indexes")
465	        claimed = local_ids | external_ids
466	        if is_uri(program["uri"]):
467	            claimed.add(program["uri"])
468	        family_ids = {
469	            family: {
470	                row["uri"] for row in item_lists[family]
471	                if isinstance(row, dict) and is_uri(row.get("uri"))
472	            }
473	            for family in ("clauses", "residuals")
474	        }
475	        for row in rows:
476	            record = row["uri"] if isinstance(row, dict) and is_uri(row.get("uri")) else root
477	            if not exact_keys(row, FRAME_INDEX_KEYS, issues, record, "frame_index"):
478	                continue
479	            if not is_uri(row["uri"]):
480	                diagnostic(issues, "invalid_uri", root, "frame_indexes.uri", str(row["uri"]))
481	            elif row["uri"] in claimed:
482	                diagnostic(issues, "duplicate_identity", record, "uri", row["uri"])
483	            else:
484	                claimed.add(row["uri"])
485	            if row["frame_ref"] not in frames:

487	            if not isinstance(row["scope"], str) or not row["scope"].strip():

489	            roots: list[str] = []

492	                roots.extend(refs)

496	                        diagnostic(issues, code, record, field, ref)
497	            if not roots:

501	    return report(program, issues, resolved_sources)

526	            )

529	        "kind": "axiom-indexer.validation-report",

534	        "resolved_sources": [
535	            {"uri": uri, "sha256": resolved_sources[uri]}

537	        ],
538	        "derived_counts": {
539	            key: len(safe_program.get(key, []))
540	            if isinstance(safe_program.get(key), list)
541	            else 0
542	            for key in ("symbols", "clauses", "residuals")
543	        },

548	def instantiate(program: dict[str, Any], validation: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
549	    outgoing: dict[str, list[str]] = {
550	        row["uri"]: []
551	        for family in ("symbols", "clauses", "residuals")
552	        for row in program[family]
553	    }
554	    for clause in program["clauses"]:
555	        for argument in clause["arguments"]:
556	            ref = argument.get("ref")
557	            if ref in outgoing:
558	                outgoing[ref].append(clause["uri"])
559	    for refs in outgoing.values():
560	        refs.sort()
561	    result = {
562	        "kind": "axiom-indexer.logical-constraint-map",
563	        "schema_version": 1,
564	        "program_uri": program["uri"],
565	        "program_sha256": validation["program_sha256"],
566	        "calculus_ref": program["calculus_ref"],
567	        "source_basis": program["source_basis"],
568	        "frame_refs": program["frame_refs"],
569	        "vocabulary_refs": program["vocabulary_refs"],
570	        "resolved_sources": validation["resolved_sources"],
571	        "symbols": {
572	            row["uri"]: {"kind": row["kind"], "label": row["label"]}
573	            for row in program["symbols"]
574	        },
575	        "clauses": program["clauses"],
576	        "constraints": [
577	            row["uri"]
578	            for row in program["clauses"]
579	            if row["clause_type"] == "constraint"
580	        ],
581	        "outgoing_clause_refs": outgoing,
582	        "residuals": program["residuals"],
583	        "source_routes": {
584	            row["uri"]: row["source_refs"]
585	            for family in ("symbols", "clauses", "residuals")
586	            for row in program[family]
587	        },
588	    }
589	    if "frame_indexes" in program:
590	        result["frame_indexes"] = {
591	            row["uri"]: row for row in program["frame_indexes"]
592	        }
593	    result["map_sha256"] = sha256(canonical_bytes(result))
594	    return result

597	def reference_closure(program: dict[str, Any], indexes: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
598	    """Close explicit local references and affected residuals, without interpreting roles."""
599	    families = {
600	        row["uri"]: family
601	        for family in ("symbols", "clauses", "residuals")
602	        for row in program[family]
603	    }
604	    items = {
605	        row["uri"]: row
606	        for family in ("symbols", "clauses", "residuals")
607	        for row in program[family]
608	    }
609	    affected: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
610	    for residual in program["residuals"]:
611	        for subject in residual["subject_refs"]:
612	            affected.setdefault(subject, []).append(residual["uri"])
613	    pending = [ref for row in indexes for field in ("clause_refs", "residual_refs") for ref in row[field]]
614	    included: set[str] = set()
615	    while pending:
616	        uri = pending.pop()
617	        if uri in included:
618	            continue
619	        included.add(uri)
620	        item = items[uri]
621	        if families[uri] == "clauses":
622	            pending.extend(arg["ref"] for arg in item["arguments"] if arg.get("ref") in items)
623	        elif families[uri] == "residuals":
624	            pending.extend(item["subject_refs"])
625	        pending.extend(affected.get(uri, []))
626	    return {
627	        family: sorted(uri for uri in included if families[uri] == family)
628	        for family in ("symbols", "clauses", "residuals")
629	    }

645	def project_program(
646	    program: Any,
647	    logical_map: Any,
648	    resolver: Resolver,
649	    index_refs: Any,
650	    mode: Any,
651	) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any] | None]:
652	    validation = validate_program(program, resolver)
653	    issues = list(validation["diagnostics"])
654	    root = validation["program_uri"] or "urn:axiom-indexer:diagnostic:program"
655	    selected: list[str] = []
656	    if not isinstance(mode, str) or mode not in PROJECTION_MODES:
657	        diagnostic(issues, "invalid_projection_mode", root, "mode", str(mode))
658	    if not isinstance(index_refs, list) or not index_refs:
659	        diagnostic(issues, "empty_selection", root, "frame_index_refs")
660	    else:
661	        for ref in index_refs:
662	            if not is_uri(ref):
663	                diagnostic(issues, "invalid_uri", root, "frame_index_refs", str(ref))
664	            elif ref in selected:
665	                diagnostic(issues, "duplicate_selection", root, "frame_index_refs", ref)
666	            else:
667	                selected.append(ref)
668	    if validation["status"] != "valid":
669	        return projection_report(program, logical_map, selected, issues), None
670	    indexes = {row["uri"]: row for row in program.get("frame_indexes", [])}
671	    other_ids = {row["uri"] for family in ("symbols", "clauses", "residuals") for row in program[family]}
672	    other_ids.update(program["frame_refs"])
673	    other_ids.update(program["vocabulary_refs"])
674	    other_ids.add(program["uri"])
675	    for ref in selected:
676	        if ref not in indexes:
677	            code = "wrong_selection_kind" if ref in other_ids else "unknown_frame_index"
678	            diagnostic(issues, code, root, "frame_index_refs", ref)
679	    expected = instantiate(program, validation)
680	    try:
681	        same_map = canonical_bytes(logical_map) == canonical_bytes(expected)
682	    except (ValueError, TypeError, UnicodeEncodeError):
683	        same_map = False
684	    if not same_map:
685	        diagnostic(issues, "map_mismatch", root, "map")
686	        if isinstance(logical_map, dict) and logical_map.get("resolved_sources") != validation["resolved_sources"]:
687	            diagnostic(issues, "source_observation_mismatch", root, "map.resolved_sources")
688	    if issues:
689	        return projection_report(program, logical_map, selected, issues), None
690	
691	    chosen = [indexes[uri] for uri in sorted(selected)]
692	    closure = reference_closure(program, chosen)
693	    rows = {
694	        family: [row for row in program[family] if row["uri"] in closure[family]]
695	        for family in closure
696	    }
697	    frames = {row["frame_ref"] for row in chosen}
698	    vocabulary = {row["kind"] for row in rows["symbols"]}
699	    sources = {program["calculus_ref"]}
700	    for row in chosen:
701	        sources.update(row["source_refs"])
702	    for family_rows in rows.values():
703	        for row in family_rows:
704	            sources.update(row["source_refs"])
705	    for row in rows["clauses"]:
706	        vocabulary.add(row["operator"])
707	        for arg in row["arguments"]:
708	            vocabulary.add(arg["role"])
709	            if arg.get("ref") in program["vocabulary_refs"]:
710	                vocabulary.add(arg["ref"])
711	            if arg.get("ref") in program["frame_refs"]:
712	                frames.add(arg["ref"])
713	    for row in rows["residuals"]:
714	        sources.update(row["re_entry_refs"])
715	        frames.update(ref for ref in row["re_entry_refs"] if ref in program["frame_refs"])
716	    sources.update(frames)
717	    result = {
718	        "kind": "axiom-indexer.frame-projection",
719	        "schema_version": 1,
720	        "mode": mode,
721	        "program_uri": program["uri"],
722	        "program_sha256": validation["program_sha256"],
723	        "map_sha256": expected["map_sha256"],
724	        "calculus_ref": program["calculus_ref"],
725	        "source_basis": program["source_basis"],
726	        "frame_indexes": chosen,
727	        "frame_refs": sorted(frames),
728	        "vocabulary_refs": sorted(vocabulary),
729	        "closure": closure,
730	        "clause_relations": [
731	            {key: row[key] for key in ("uri", "clause_type", "operator", "arguments")}
732	            for row in rows["clauses"]
733	        ],
734	        "residual_routes": [
735	            {key: row[key] for key in ("uri", "kind", "subject_refs", "re_entry_refs")}
736	            for row in rows["residuals"]
737	        ],
738	        "source_routes": {
739	            row["uri"]: row["source_refs"]
740	            for row in chosen + [row for family_rows in rows.values() for row in family_rows]
741	        },
742	        "resolved_sources": [row for row in validation["resolved_sources"] if row["uri"] in sources],
743	    }
744	    if mode == "materialized":
745	        result.update(rows)
746	    result["projection_sha256"] = sha256(canonical_bytes(result))
747	    return projection_report(program, logical_map, selected, []), copy.deepcopy(result)

750	def join_sections(sections: Any) -> str:
751	    if not isinstance(sections, list):
752	        raise ValueError("invalid_sections")
753	    parts: list[str] = []
754	    for section in sections:
755	        if not isinstance(section, dict) or set(section) != {"label", "text"}:
756	            raise ValueError("invalid_section")
757	        label = section["label"]
758	        text = section["text"]
759	        if not isinstance(label, str) or not isinstance(text, str):
760	            raise ValueError("invalid_section")
761	        parts.append(label + "\n" + text)
762	    result = "\n\n".join(parts)
763	    try:
764	        result.encode("utf-8")
765	    except UnicodeEncodeError as exc:
766	        raise ValueError("invalid_section_encoding") from exc
767	    return result

821	    """Overapproximate URI targets before any output effect, including invalid input."""
822	    pending = [program]
823	    refs: set[str] = set()
824	    while pending:
825	        value = pending.pop()
826	        if isinstance(value, dict):
827	            pending.extend(value.values())
828	        elif isinstance(value, list):
829	            pending.extend(value)
830	        elif is_uri(value):
831	            refs.add(value)
832	    for ref in sorted(refs):
833	        try:
834	            resolver.resolve(ref)
835	        except (OSError, UnicodeError, ValueError, RuntimeError):
836	            # Known targets are protected before confinement/fragment refusal.
837	            # A failed physical resolution leaves protection incomplete.
838	            pass

841	def write_projection(path: Path, value: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
842	    temporary: Path | None = None
843	    try:
844	        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=path.parent, prefix=".axiom-projection-", delete=False) as handle:
845	            temporary = Path(handle.name)
846	            handle.write(canonical_bytes(value) + b"\n")
847	        os.replace(temporary, path)
848	        temporary = None
849	    finally:
850	        if temporary is not None:
851	            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)

854	def project_cli(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
855	    inputs = [args.program, args.map, args.bindings]
856	    program: Any = None
857	    logical_map: Any = None
858	    resolver: Resolver | None = None
859	    source_safety = False
860	    selected = args.frame_index or []
861	    issues: list[dict[str, str]] = []
862	    root = "urn:axiom-indexer:diagnostic:projection"
863	    exit_code = 1
864	    result: dict[str, Any] | None = None
865	    try:
866	        program = load_json(args.program)
867	        resolver = Resolver(args.bindings, load_json(args.bindings))
868	        protect_program_sources(program, resolver)
869	        source_safety = resolver.protection_complete
870	        logical_map = load_json(args.map)
871	        evaluation, result = project_program(program, logical_map, resolver, selected, args.mode)
872	        issues.extend(evaluation["diagnostics"])
873	    except (OSError, UnicodeError, json.JSONDecodeError, DuplicateKeyError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError) as exc:
874	        diagnostic(issues, "input_error", root, "input", str(exc))
875	        exit_code = 2
876	
877	    source_safety = source_safety and resolver is not None and resolver.protection_complete
878	    safe_output = source_safety
879	    if args.output is not None:
880	        protected = inputs + list(resolver.protected_paths if resolver is not None else [])
881	        try:
882	            if any(path_alias(args.output, source) for source in protected):
883	                diagnostic(issues, "input_output_path_alias", root, "output", str(args.output))
884	                safe_output = False
885	                exit_code = 2
886	            elif not source_safety:
887	                diagnostic(issues, "output_safety_unresolved", root, "output", str(args.output))
888	                exit_code = 2
889	        except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
890	            diagnostic(issues, "output_safety_unresolved", root, "output", str(exc))
891	            safe_output = False
892	            exit_code = 2
893	
894	    if not issues and result is not None:
895	        try:
896	            if args.output is None:
897	                write_json(None, result)
898	            else:
899	                write_projection(args.output, result)
900	                write_json(None, projection_report(program, logical_map, selected, []))
901	            return 0
902	        except (OSError, ValueError, UnicodeError) as exc:
903	            diagnostic(issues, "output_error", root, "output", str(exc))
904	            exit_code = 2
905	    if args.output is not None and safe_output:
906	        try:
907	            clear_stale_map(args.output)
908	        except OSError as exc:
909	            diagnostic(issues, "stale_output_removal_failed", root, "output", str(exc))
910	            exit_code = 2

915	def main() -> int:
916	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
917	    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

932	    project_parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
933	    args = parser.parse_args()
934	
935	    if args.command == "project":
936	        return project_cli(args)
937	
938	    if args.command == "join":
939	        if args.output is not None and path_alias(args.input, args.output):
940	            print("join_error:input_output_path_alias", file=sys.stderr)
941	            return 2
942	        try:
943	            sections = load_json(args.input)
944	            joined = join_sections(sections)
945	        except (
946	            OSError,

949	            DuplicateKeyError,
950	            ValueError,
951	        ) as exc:
952	            print(f"join_error:{exc}", file=sys.stderr)
953	            return 2
954	        write_text(args.output, joined)
955	        return 0

957	    inputs = [args.program, args.bindings]
958	    outputs = [path for path in (args.output, args.emit_map) if path]
959	    input_alias = any(
960	        path_alias(output, source) for output in outputs for source in inputs
961	    )

963	    if input_alias or output_alias:

965	            path_alias(args.emit_map, source) for source in inputs
966	        ):
967	            clear_stale_map(args.emit_map)
968	        write_json(None, input_failure("input_output_path_alias"))
969	        return 2

971	        program = load_json(args.program)
972	        binding_value = load_json(args.bindings)

974	        validation = validate_program(program, resolver)
975	    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, DuplicateKeyError, ValueError) as exc:

979	        return 2

1	# STDO Reference Frame Baseline
2	
3	## Canonical Compression
4	
5	`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md` defines the finite engagement atom. The selected
6	complete STDO cut defines specification, design, construction, assessment,
7	disposition, checkpoint, continuation, identity, and release law. This profile
8	maps three practical engagement frames onto those existing owners:
9	
10	```text
11	existing project authority
12	  + selected complete STDO and Reference Frame Method basis
13	  + exact governed Product or Product-chain outcome and workspace basis
14	  + known evaluation inventory, dependencies, and residuals
15	  -> sufficient direct Worker activation, or materially required coordination
16	  -> where coordinated: Executive outcome/basis lock and finite ready frontier
17	  -> Worker and applicable specialist evaluations; Reviewer only where required
18	  -> closed results, applicable technical triage, and declared conjunction
19	  -> existing bounded decision authority, result recording, and next lawful action
20	  -> updated basis, coverage, residuals, and frontier
21	  -> repeat or stop
22	```
23	
24	The three available frames are overlapping evaluation contexts, not a hierarchy
25	or actor topology. The Worker supplies the candidate subject but never activates the
26	Reviewer. The Reviewer evaluates but does not implement. The Executive applies
27	only decision authority already granted by Product, Goals, requirements,
28	accepted design, ticket, identity, or release law. The Worker carries only the
29	construction or transformation authority in its admitted intake. No frame gains
30	admission, publication, mutation, or other operation authority from its label.
31	
32	This profile also derives twelve generic specialist-frame families: Product,
33	Product Composition, Design, Design Component, Public Boundary, Entity,
34	Operator, Owner, Effect, Reuse/Foundation, Install, and Proof. They separate recurring evaluation
35	questions that otherwise collapse across constitutional `WHAT`, structural
36	`HOW`, identity, authority, effects, foundations, installed subjects, and
37	evidence. They are available frame families, not mandatory actors, stages,
38	components, services, files, or runtime types. An activation selects only the
39	families material to its exact evaluation and retains an explicit residual for
40	any material family it cannot cover.
41	
42	This profile also derives four Product-testing specialist-frame families:
43	user acceptance, end to end, integration, and unit. They are activated inside
44	the same conditionally selected engagement relation; they are not new
45	roles, stages, authorities, or a testing hierarchy. Their ordinary evidence
46	topology is:
47	
48	```text
49	Product and accepted design
50	  |- user-outcome claims -> user-acceptance frames
51	  |- runnable causal-path claims -> end-to-end frames
52	  |- composition-boundary claims -> integration frames
53	  `- module-owned laws -> unit frames
54	
55	bound results -> declared conjunction -> Product or release disposition
56	```
57	
58	The fan-out assigns claims to their congruent evidence frames; it is not an
59	authority hierarchy or a claim that one frame decomposes into another.
60	Evidence may relate through declared conjunction, translation, falsification,
61	and re-entry. A broader frame cannot make a module-owned law true, and any
62	number of narrower green frames cannot establish an unevaluated Product
63	composition or user outcome.
64	
65	A project may adopt this profile or define another reference-frame
66	configuration. That choice is admitted by the existing project authority that
67	owns the affected decision. A local axioms file may carry the decision; the file
68	does not become a new constitutional owner merely by carrying it.
69	
70	---
71	
72	## Status And Authority Boundary
73	
74	This document is an optional derived role and evaluation profile. It has no
75	independent ownership of STDO's execution protocol or of any Product binding.
76	
77	The ownership layers are distinct:
78	
79	- `REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md` owns the pure frame principles;
80	- this profile owns the optional Executive, Worker, Reviewer, specialist, and
81	  testing mappings; and
82	- `SPEC_METHOD.md#collective-reference-frame-basis` owns the Product-binding
83	  relation, while each adopting Product authority owns its concrete Project
84	  Reference-Frame Basis.
85	
86	| Relation | Normative owner | Use in this profile |
87	|---|---|---|
88	| frame declaration, activation, result algebra, conjunction, translation, coverage, and revision | `REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md` | defines each engagement frame and the active configuration |
89	| bounded-frame conservation and execution intake | `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` `STDO-UP-017..019`; `SPEC_METHOD.md` `STDO-UP-020` | supplies the Worker activation basis |
90	| construction, self-review, assessment, disposition, checkpoint, and continuation | `SPEC_METHOD.md` `STDO-UP-020` | supplies the complete execution transition relation |
91	| author/implementer and independent-review separation | `TICKET_METHOD.md` `STDO-UP-007` | supplies Reviewer independence and exact-verdict traceability |
92	| exact assurance subject, evidence population, and generic-method freeze | `SPEC_METHOD.md` `STDO-UP-022` | supplies review-boundary and qualification constraints |
93	| module-derived unit proof | `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` Design-to-Module evidence route and Module-Derived Unit Test Rule | supplies the unit frame's module ownership basis while this profile limits its claim and evidence altitude |
94	| capability and foundation selection before material generic construction | `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md` `STDO-UP-023` | supplies the Worker's proportional reuse comparison without treating reuse itself as authority transfer; any assigned foundation role preserves its declared relation and owner |
95	| Product testing taxonomy, claim, ordinary user path, and acceptance meaning | `SPEC_METHOD.md` Verification Layers, Testing Strategy Taxonomy, and Test Authority Rule; current Product, requirements, accepted design, and release authority where applicable | selects user outcomes, supported interfaces, material compositions, runnable Product subjects, harnessed or live execution mode, and required testing populations |
96	| generic Product, Product Composition, Design, Design Component, Public Boundary, Entity, Operator, Owner, Effect, Reuse/Foundation, Install, and Proof evaluation families | current Product and requirements; `SPEC_METHOD.md` composition law; accepted design; `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md`; `IDENTITY_METHOD.md`; `RELEASE_METHOD.md`; applicable domain, effect, interface, dependency, and assurance owners | supplies recurring specialist evaluation families without transferring their owners or requiring one architecture |
97	| work selection and growth authority | current Goals, Product, requirements, and admitted ticket or equivalent work authority | selects the governed outcome and admits local frame configuration |
98	| design structure and local realization frame decisions | accepted design under its governing Product and requirements | supplies specialist frames and material relations |
99	| human and proxy identity | `IDENTITY_METHOD.md` plus project authority | binds the Executive actor and its decision envelope |
100	| Product and release acceptance | current Product and `RELEASE_METHOD.md` | retains direct acceptance where those owners require it |
101	
102	Every requirement in this profile is either:
103	
104	1. an exact application of a cited owning STDO relation; or
105	2. a condition for claiming adoption of this optional profile.
106	
107	Neither kind creates a second amendment path for the owning federal law. If the
108	profile conflicts with an owning STDO clause, the owning clause controls and the
109	profile requires revision.
110	
111	Inclusion in an exact released standards cut or another admitted method basis
112	makes this profile available; it does not adopt it. Adoption requires a
113	separately accepted Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis. Mutable
114	authoring source, installed file presence, prompts, summaries, and commentary
115	neither select nor adopt it.
116	
117	---
118	
119	## Engagement Applicability
120	
121	This profile applies `SPEC_METHOD.md#construction-assessment-and-delegation`
122	and the selected Product-owned frame configuration. One capable context with
123	sufficient work authority, intake and operation grant may enter directly as
124	Worker (Writer). It needs no Executive activation solely to appoint it.
125	Coordination activates when material contexts, authority, capability or
126	required independence cannot be covered by that sufficient direct activation.
127	A role or frame name alone creates no coordination or review obligation.
128	
129	The direct route binds the same exact intake, operation territory, applicable
130	obligations, evidence, stop conditions and declared result consumer. It uses
131	the smallest existing carrier under `TICKET_METHOD.md`, retaining admission
132	distinct from drafting. A sufficient local outcome with no required independent
133	assessment or reserved acceptance may finish as Writer and record its satisfied
134	conditions there. It gains no review, ticket, diagram recreation or owner
135	ceremony solely from using this profile. Any required assessment or owner
136	decision remains required; newly discovered insufficiency withholds the
137	dependent effect and returns the affected question to its existing owner.
138	
139	The Executive transition and handoff clauses below apply when that coordinated
140	branch is selected. Direct work returns its closed result to the declared work
141	authority or existing result carrier, preserving the same result algebra and
142	operation/decision separation. In either branch, apply
143	`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#applicability-and-required-results` and reuse valid
144	C/J/O through their owning SPEC_METHOD and TICKET_METHOD clauses. None of these
145	routes alters a Product's exact adopted basis or supplies missing authority.
146	
147	## Empirical Revision Boundary
148	
149	Accumulated delivery practice and observed failure may inform frame selection,
150	qualification, and revision. Such evidence does not become STDO authority and
151	does not import the originating consumer's architecture, names, actors,
152	topology, runtime, artifacts, or work stages into this generic profile.
153	
154	The profile's engagement relation requires:
155	
156	- one bounded authority selects the active work and the finite frames needed to
157	  evaluate it;
158	- a Worker constructs one exact candidate, self-reviews, reports, and stops;
159	- where independent assessment is required, a separately activated Reviewer
160	  acquires sufficient exact live authority, subject and evidence, retaining
161	  valid computed facts while supplying its own judgment;
162	- an activated Reviewer returns evidence-bound severity and technical
163	  implications without becoming a second implementation loop;
164	- where coordination is required, Executive assigns priority and adjudicates
165	  the current Product mandate under an existing bounded grant; and
166	- inability to perceive a known violation is evidence of a missing,
167	  misactivated, oversized, or capability-incompatible frame.
168	
169	Repeated resets, extended repair loops, moving review subjects, proof masking,
170	and duplicate authority are generic signals that a frame declaration,
171	activation, capability match, basis, or authority relation may be defective.
172	They justify reevaluation; they do not identify one universal architecture or
173	grant precedent semantic authority.
174	
175	The same applies to repeated Product drift: a useful implementation,
176	specialization, scenario, dependency, installed builder, or downstream Product
177	does not become the Product being authored merely because it is visible to the
178	same actor or participates in one delivery chain.
179	
180	---
181	
182	## Profile Terms
183	
184	### Engagement frame
185	
186	An **engagement frame** is a `REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md` frame whose evaluation
187	family concerns selection, construction, assessment, or disposition of governed
188	work. Executive, Worker, and Reviewer are this profile's engagement frames.
189	
190	### Specialist frame
191	
192	A **specialist frame** is an activated Product, requirement, design, identity,
193	release, domain, implementation, test, operational, historical, or capability
194	frame needed by one engagement evaluation. A method member, file, component, or
195	lens becomes a frame only when its evaluation, basis, material manifold,
196	authority, evidence, result algebra, and capability envelope are declared.
197	
198	### Generic specialist-frame family
199	
200	A **generic specialist-frame family** is a reusable evaluation-family
201	archetype in this profile. It identifies a recurring distinction that a
202	project must either instantiate it where material, have capable authority
203	establish it as non-material for the governed outcome, or retain it as an
204	explicit coverage residual.
205	
206	The family does not select a concrete carrier, component, actor, architecture,
207	owner, or implementation. One project may instantiate several frames in one
208	family. One declared frame may cover several families only when its evaluation
209	and result relations preserve every material distinction rather than flattening
210	them behind one broad label.
211	
212	### Testing frame
213	
214	A **testing frame** is a specialist frame whose evaluation executes or observes
215	a declared subject to discriminate one exact claim through an explicit oracle,
216	evidence population, path boundary, and falsification condition. A test file,
217	suite, runner, fixture, scenario label, coverage percentage, or actor does not
218	become a testing frame merely by existing.
219	
220	Testing-frame authority is bounded by the claim actually exercised. Test count,
221	assertion count, source coverage, runtime duration, and framework category do
222	not widen that boundary.
223	
224	### Authoritative Product path
225	
226	An **authoritative Product path** is the declared ordinary causal composition
227	from a supported user or Public entry through the exact selected interfaces,
228	owners, state transitions, effects, persistence and recovery boundaries, and
229	outcome projection required by the Product claim. Producing an expected output
230	through a bypass, obsolete executor, test-only seam, undeclared fallback, or
231	competing authority falsifies path conformance even when the output value is
232	equal.
233	
234	### Material combinatorial complexity
235	
236	**Material combinatorial complexity** is the claim-relative population of
237	independent dimensions and interactions whose combinations can change an
238	outcome, violate an invariant, select another authority path, or expose a
239	failure. At unit altitude it includes module-owned laws, including behavior at
240	the public module contract, and their algebraic operators, calculation regimes,
241	states, transitions, boundary classes, and failure cases. Cross-participant
242	interface, Product, persistence, configuration, and user-role combinations
243	belong to integration, end-to-end, or user-acceptance frames rather than being
244	mocked away and counted as unit evidence.
245	
246	### Executive
247	
248	**Executive** is the profile label for the frame that selects or confirms the
249	bounded activation configuration and consumes closed Worker and Reviewer
250	results under existing project decision authority. It holds the complete
251	Product view and current MVP or release mandate needed to assign priority,
252	apply disposition, and select the next authorized action.
253	
254	It may be occupied by direct human authority or by a bounded proxy admitted
255	under `STDO-UP-020`, `IDENTITY_METHOD.md`, and the current project authority.
256	It is not a universal semantic owner, controller, manager service, or runtime
257	executive observer.
258	
259	---
260	
261	## Executive Attention, Evaluation, And Action
262	
263	Executive is the profile frame for three inseparable duties over one governed
264	outcome:
265	
266	1. **attention management** maintains the exact outcome and basis, Product-role
267	   map, evaluation inventory, dependency relation, unresolved frontier, actor
268	   envelopes, current MVP or release mandate, applicable triage policy, and
269	   residual boundary, then selects the smallest
270	   dependency-ready activation set sufficient for the next decision within the
271	   finite actor envelopes;
272	2. **evaluation orchestration** activates capable Workers, Reviewers, or
273	   specialists, preserves their exact subjects and bases, and consumes only
274	   closed results or declared translations; and
275	3. **authorized action selection** assigns priority, determines the effect on
276	   the current promotion boundary, applies an existing disposition, and issues
277	   only the next already-authorized activation or action.
278	
279	Executive does not contain the complete workspace, perform every evaluation,
280	or acquire Product meaning, implementation, mutation, acceptance, publication,
281	or other operation authority from the role. A material effect remains owned by
282	the actor carrying its exact operation grant.
283	
284	An actor occupying Executive must not modify candidate, Product or worktree
285	bytes or perform an implementation effect. Filesystem or tool access and an
286	edit being small, test-only, reversible or apparently obvious supply no
287	exception. Mutation requires a separately activated Worker or Writer relation
288	with the exact operation grant, subject and write territory. A same-actor role
289	transition is explicit and recorded in the existing work carrier before the
290	effect; the actor is no longer acting as Executive for that effect. Recording
291	or delegating after an Executive edit cannot authorize it retroactively.
292	
293	The attention cycle is:
294	
295	```text
296	U0 = every known material evaluation not closed on the current basis
297	
298	while U is non-empty:
299	  select a finite dependency-ready subset M that fits the assigned actors
300	  activate each member of M against the exact outcome and basis
301	  keep assurance-independent evaluations free of unclosed peer results
302	  record every closed result, technical triage, residual, and invalidation condition
303	  apply only declared conjunctions or translations
304	  assign priority and boundary effect only under the current Product mandate
305	  invalidate affected results when the subject or basis changes
306	  update U from coverage, dependencies, conflicts, and discovered materiality
307	
308	stop only when every mandatory evaluation is closed, or governing authority
309	has explicitly retained every remaining residual consistently with the claim
310	```
311	
312	This relation requires no scheduler or frame engine. `M` may contain parallel
313	activations. Recursion follows declared evaluation dependencies and bounded
314	refinements; it does not nest or join undifferentiated copies of every frame.
315	The Executive retains the frontier and closed-result ledger in attention, not
316	the undocumented working context of every evaluator.
317	
318	Severity supplied by Reviewer is evaluation evidence. Priority, current-boundary
319	effect, `STDO-UP-020` disposition, and subsequent action are Executive decisions.
320	They remain distinct ledger entries even when a Product-defined policy maps one
321	to another.
322	
323	Every result returns to Executive, a declared conjunction, or another frame
324	through an explicit `D` relation. No lateral handoff, child completion, model
325	response, tool output, or shared actor implicitly activates another frame or
326	authorizes continuation. A consumer receives the closed result and its source
327	routes, not the child's hidden reasoning context.
328	
329	### Executive Drift Locks
330	
331	Before activation and before disposition, Executive revalidates:
332	
333	- **outcome lock** — selected Goal, Product outcome, boundary, and lawful
334	  re-entry class, current MVP or release mandate, and triage policy remain
335	  unchanged;
336	- **basis lock** — subject, authority, dependency, configuration, topology,
337	  evidence, time, and candidate coordinates remain exact and current;
338	- **Product-role lock** — mutable Source Project, Product Definition,
339	  Release Cut, Product, Install, Artifact, and dependent Product identities
340	  remain distinct, and every Development Product role remains bound to its
341	  exact underlying Install;
342	- **authority lock** — semantic, evaluation, operation, decision, acceptance,
343	  and publication owners and grants remain unchanged; and
344	- **coverage-and-return lock** — every material evaluation and interaction is
345	  closed or explicit residual, and every consumed result followed its declared
346	  return relation.
347	
348	Changed Product meaning requires re-entry. A stale or substituted basis is
349	`invalid_basis`. Missing material scope is `out_of_frame`. Missing operation
350	authority refuses activation or the effect. An unresolved mandatory conflict
351	prevents a satisfied conjunction. Executive does not repair any of these by
352	making its own frame larger.
353	
354	### Product-Chain Basis
355	
356	A governed outcome may concern one Product or an explicit directed chain of
357	Products. Its basis records the distinct role of every mutable Source Project,
358	current Product Definition, exact candidate checkpoint, Release Cut, Product,
359	Install, Artifact, Development Product, dependent Product, and composition
360	edge. Each Development Product role binds one exact underlying Install
361	identity. Each edge names its source and target roles, governing authority and
362	contracts, lifecycle, evidence boundary, refusal, and invalidation.
363	
364	An installed Product may lawfully build its own successor or another Product.
365	That Development Product remains distinct from the mutable Source Project and
366	the Product being authored. Directory nesting, shared code, shared actors,
367	source imports, tool reachability, matching labels, or output equality creates
368	no Product identity, composition edge, or authority transfer.
369	
370	Exact basis does not make a Source Project immutable. A Worker may
371	cumulatively mutate the exact Source Project and write territory named by its
372	operation grant. A Reviewer evaluates an exact candidate checkpoint produced
373	from that workspace. Repair advances the workspace, creates a new candidate,
374	and invalidates affected results. A released Product, Release Cut, or exact
375	Install remains immutable under its own lifecycle law; it does not impose
376	immutability on the Source Project constructing a successor.
377	
378	### Worker
379	
380	**Worker** is the profile label for `STDO-UP-020`'s bounded constructor role
381	when activated as a reference frame. It owns construction and self-review
382	inside its exact intake through the operation authority inherited from the
383	governing work relation. It does not acquire admission, publication, acceptance,
384	or continuation authority.
385	
386	### Reviewer
387	
388	**Reviewer** is the profile label for the independent live-surface evaluation
389	consumed by the `STDO-UP-020` assessment relation and governed by
390	`STDO-UP-007` and `STDO-UP-022` when activated as a reference frame. It
391	evaluates one exact subject and returns a closed result with evidence-bound
392	technical triage when a finding exists. It does not implement the repair,
393	assign priority, apply disposition, or activate the next frame.
394	
395	### Technical triage, severity, priority, and boundary effect
396	
397	**Technical triage** is the Reviewer-owned assessment of one finding against
398	the exact evaluated claim and basis. Where supported by admissible evidence and
399	the actor capability envelope, it records:
400	
401	- the affected claim and observed failure;
402	- severity under the Product-selected severity scale;
403	- causal assessment and confidence;
404	- blast radius and affected users, paths, or relations;
405	- available workaround or containment;
406	- repair complexity, regression risk, and material dependencies; and
407	- residual uncertainty and the evidence required to reduce it.
408	
409	Missing causal or repair evidence remains explicit. Reviewer returns
410	`indeterminate` or `out_of_frame` pressure where the missing relation can change
411	the evaluation; it does not invent precision or send work laterally to Worker.
412	
413	**Severity** grades consequence if the finding manifests. **Priority** orders
414	response relative to the complete Product outcome, likelihood and exposure,
415	current MVP or release mandate, reversibility, dependencies, cost of delay, and
416	available capacity. Reviewer grades severity. Executive assigns priority.
417	
418	The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis binds the severity scale,
419	priority scale, current-boundary decision cutoff, and non-waivable hard stops.
420	This profile imposes no universal numeric scale. Severity, priority, Reference
421	Frame Method result, and current-boundary effect remain distinct. None alone
422	makes a finding release-blocking.
423	
424	**Current-boundary effect** is Executive's determination that the finding blocks
425	the current promotion boundary, requires narrowing, or may remain an explicit
426	residual. Executive then applies exactly one existing `STDO-UP-020`
427	disposition. A hard stop or falsified mandatory claim cannot be waived by
428	lowering priority. An observation outside the exact claim boundary cannot
429	create another review round merely by receiving a severe label.
430	
431	### Work result
432	
433	A **work result** is the closed Worker output to its declared consumer; in the
434	coordinated branch that consumer is Executive. It exists only after successful
435	Worker activation. An `activation_refusal` returns to the assigning authority
436	or declared result carrier and creates neither a Worker activation nor a
437	Worker result.
438	
439	The work-result variants are profile carriers, not new STDO semantic
440	dispositions. They are disjoint by their accompanying Reference Frame Method
441	result:
442	
443	- `candidate_ready` accompanies `satisfied`: an exact candidate and transition
444	  evidence are available;
445	- `refused` accompanies `falsified`: lawful activation occurred, but a
446	  governing prohibition or owner-valid construction refusal defeats the
447	  requested construction;
448	- `incomplete` accompanies `indeterminate`: the valid activation has not
449	  produced a candidate because admissible evidence or bounded execution cannot
450	  yet decide or complete the relation; and
451	- `re_entry_requested` accompanies `out_of_frame` or `invalid_basis`: a
452	  material decision lies outside Worker authority or the activated basis can no
453	  longer support the work.
454	
455	The mapping is total and exclusive after lawful activation. Payload wording,
456	stop timing, or actor preference cannot select another variant. A capability,
457	authority, stale-basis, ambiguous-basis, or topology mismatch known during
458	activation is an `activation_refusal`, not a synthetic Worker result.
459	
460	Consumers choose the representation. `STDO-UP-020` remains the owner of the
461	execution relation and its semantic dispositions.
462	
463	The result references current computed classification, supporting evidence,
464	residual judgments and original rulings through their existing owning carriers.
465	It does not reconstruct unchanged C/J/O for each handoff. The consumer checks
466	applicability and concrete invalidators; changed evidence revises only affected
467	results, preserving originals and supported surviving claims under
468	`TICKET_METHOD.md#recorded-judgment-and-owner-ruling-continuity`.
469	
470	### Exact candidate
471	
472	An **exact candidate** is the subject identity required by `STDO-UP-020`
473	transition evidence and `STDO-UP-007` review traceability. Where
474	`STDO-UP-022` generic method qualification applies, its construction result is
475	frozen before material reference exposure as that clause requires. Elsewhere,

559	### Steel-Thread Delivery
560	
561	Executive sequences delivery around a steel thread: the smallest real,
562	runnable path from a supported Product entry to a material outcome through
563	the selected composition. Establish that path early and expand it in bounded
564	increments. Where it already exists, extend or revalidate the affected
565	thread. Select increments by consequential uncertainty, dependency and
566	interface reach, and failure impact.
567	
568	Early end-to-end and integration evidence prunes incompatible construction
569	choices before they spread. Use it to settle the exercised interfaces,
570	preserve working composition, and concentrate construction on unresolved
571	obligations. Each passing thread establishes only the relations and
572	conditions actually exercised; untested branches, interaction combinations,
573	refusal and recovery paths retain their material proof obligations. Revisit
574	settled construction decisions when material counterevidence invalidates
575	their basis.
576	
577	During construction, use focused deterministic regression and targeted
578	judgment probes to resolve material uncertainty. Use unit evidence for
579	module-owned laws under the testing frames. Schedule substantial,
580	resource-intensive user-acceptance cycles near release or when a bounded
581	capability is considered complete enough to qualify. An early focused user
582	probe remains appropriate when it decides a material outcome uncertainty.
583	
584	The [Product testing frames](#derived-product-testing-frame-set) retain their
585	distinct claims and govern the necessary scenarios, independent assessments,
586	and repetitions. Reuse qualified results while their exact subject and basis
587	remain valid; rerun affected assurance when a material change invalidates it.
588	Executive selects this sequence under the existing mandate and activates
589	construction through the existing operation grants.

733	## Derived Product Testing Frame Set
734	
735	When this profile supports Product promotion, closure, or release assurance,
736	testing is configured as a claim-relative specialist-frame set. The kind of
737	runner does not select the frame. The evaluated claim, subject, path,
738	population, oracle, and falsification boundary do.
739	
740	Where the generic specialist set is adopted, testing frames supply
741	claim-congruent evidence to one or more Proof-frame evaluations. Proof is not a
742	testing hierarchy or aggregate-green frame: user-acceptance, end-to-end,
743	integration, and unit results retain their distinct claims and coordinates.
744	
745	The ordinary configuration contains four distinct frames:
746	
747	- user acceptance evaluates the Product outcome from the user's supported
748	  reference frame;
749	- end to end evaluates the complete runnable causal realization of that
750	  outcome;
751	- integration evaluates one material composition boundary and its interaction
752	  population; and
753	- unit evaluates one module-owned law. Internal combinatorial complexity
754	  determines the proportional size and strategy of that evidence, not whether
755	  the module-owned law is eligible for unit proof.
756	
757	These frames may overlap and one execution may supply evidence to several of
758	them. Every result remains bound to its own claim. A label such as `UAT`, `E2E`,
759	`integration`, or `unit` has no assurance value without the corresponding frame
760	declaration.

844	| evidence | law-derived examples, equivalence classes, finite exhaustive cases where available, property-based or generative cases, metamorphic relations, calculation or algebra oracles, boundary cases, and killed internal mutations |
845	| capability envelope | competence to derive an oracle independently from the owned law, identify the module-bounded combination population, and distinguish invariant violation from implementation restatement |
846	| exclusions | Product outcomes, cross-module composition, supported user paths, packaging or installation, real external participants, orchestration topology, mocked-away interface behavior, incidental branches, private helper layout, assertion count, and source coverage used as broader assurance |
847	| result | one Reference Frame Method result limited to the exact module-owned law and module-bounded population, with counterexamples, residual combinations, and invalidation conditions |
848	| invalidation | material Ontology, IACS, module boundary, owned law, algorithm, state space, numerical regime, implementation, oracle, generator, or module-bounded population change |

850	Unit testing is deliberately module-bounded. Every coded module requires the
851	module-derived unit lane owned by `DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD.md`; public module
852	contracts are valid unit-proof subjects. Internal combinatorial complexity
853	determines the proportional size and strategy of that evidence. Its highest
854	discriminating value is often in algebras, calculations, transformations,
855	parsers, reducers, state machines, decision tables, admission predicates,
856	conservation relations, and bounded algorithms with strong independently
857	derived oracles. A unit test whose oracle merely repeats the implementation or
858	whose cases follow incidental code branches provides weak or circular
859	evidence.
860	
861	Modules whose material complexity lies primarily in composition, orchestration,
862	configuration, persistence, ownership, or user interaction require integration,
863	end-to-end, or user-acceptance evidence at that actual boundary. Mocking those
864	relations into a unit test does not convert their complexity into unit evidence.
865	
866	This profile does not waive the module-derived unit lane. It binds that lane to
867	module-owned law and the smallest congruent evidence population. Low internal
868	combinatorial complexity justifies a small lane, not omission and not hundreds
869	of implementation-shaped tests. Unit-test volume has no independent closure
870	value.
871	
872	No Product, user-outcome, installed-path, cross-module composition, or release
873	claim may be closed from unit evidence, regardless of test count, assertion
874	count, source coverage, mutation score, runtime, or historical pass rate.
875	Treating unit green as broader assurance is a frame error.
876	
877	### Combinatorial Coverage And Testing-Value Index
878	
879	Testing value is indexed first by the material combinations a frame can
880	discriminate for its exact claim. It is not indexed by test, assertion, file,
881	line, branch, mock, snapshot, or runner count.
882	
883	For one claim, the testing-value index considers at least:
884	
885	1. congruence between the claim and evaluated subject;
886	2. the number and materiality of independent claim dimensions;
887	3. the interaction strength actually covered among those dimensions;
888	4. authoritative-path exactness;
889	5. oracle independence and precision;
890	6. sensitivity to realistic faults, rival paths, and historical failures;
891	7. observability, reconstruction, and reproducibility of the result; and
892	8. explicit residual combinations and invalidation conditions.
893	
894	No universal scalar is required. A project may define one only through Product,
895	requirement, or accepted-design authority and must retain the underlying
896	coverage coordinates rather than flattening them into a score.
897	
898	At unit altitude, the relevant dimensions are module-bounded. Unit-testing
899	value normally rises with the internal combinatorial complexity of an algebra,
900	calculation, state machine, transition relation, or other module-owned closed
901	domain because local tests can cheaply discriminate many meaningful
902	combinations against a precise oracle.
903	
904	At integration, end-to-end, and user-acceptance altitude, testing value can be
905	multiplicative rather than additive: each material interface composes
906	preconditions, postconditions, authority, state, configuration, failure, and
907	recovery with every other traversed boundary. The evidence value comes from
908	the interactions actually discriminated, not from merely touching many
909	interfaces on one sunny path.
910	
911	Material Product factors commonly include:
912	
913	- user role and capability;
914	- supported operation and Product composition;
915	- selected definition, owner, implementation, and dependency;
916	- lifecycle and persisted state;
917	- configuration and version combination;
918	- process, continuation, retry, re-entry, and recovery mode;
919	- success, refusal, malformed result, partial failure, and competing-path case;
920	- fresh-process, replay, reconstruction, and migration condition; and
921	- user-visible outcome and projection.
922	
923	The activated frame declares the finite interaction population and why its
924	covering set is adequate. Pairwise or other covering-array reduction is lawful
925	only where the basis explains why omitted higher-order interactions cannot
926	change the claim or retains them as residuals. High-consequence authority,
927	persistence, concurrency, recovery, migration, and historically failure-prone
928	relations normally require explicit higher-strength combinations.
929	
930	Source, line, branch, and function coverage may diagnose whether code was
931	visited. They do not establish semantic combination coverage, authoritative
932	path selection, user-outcome coverage, or the absence of a rival path.
933
