# The STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems

## Position

The **STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems**, written `a_c`,
is STDO's domain-specific, carrier-neutral constitutional calculus for
representing and relating governed symbolic systems.

Its stable concept identity is:

```text
urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c
```

This standard owns that concept in bounded context:

```text
urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus
```

`a_c` is a separately identifiable calculus derived from STDO principles. It
defines sorts, typed objects, relations, constraints, latitude, residual
uncertainty, traversals, functor kinds, judgments, closure, projections,
transformations, models, and validity laws. Those definitions do not depend on
a derivation-source record layout, a selected subject interpretation, a
particular carrier, a model provider, a runtime, or a repository topology.

`a_c` makes no claim of universal applicability, logical completeness,
consistency, decidability, soundness, or category-theoretic status except where
an exact, separately identified proof establishes that claim for a declared
fragment, model, or relation.

STDO principles are the derivation provenance of the calculus. Application of
the calculus to any exact subject is a separately owned downstream relation.
Those relations are distinct:

```text
exact predecessor STDO principles ──derive──> a_c
a_c + exact subject X              ──interpret──> a_c.X
a_c.X + exact accepted semantic judgment J_X
      + exact carrier C            ──encode─────> a_c.X.C
```

The calculus, an interpreted model, and an encoded carrier are distinct
governed layers with separate content identities and proof boundaries. A layer
becomes a released Product only through separately authorized Product
acceptance and release. Neither interpretation nor encoding can redefine the
calculus.

## Derivation Provenance

The calculus contracts recurring principles already established by STDO:

- scoped identity and authority conservation from
  [`IDENTITY_METHOD.md#core-law`](IDENTITY_METHOD.md#core-law) and
  [`IDENTITY_METHOD.md#authority-identity-and-conservation-stdo-up-004`](IDENTITY_METHOD.md#authority-identity-and-conservation-stdo-up-004);
- exact bounded-context meaning and explicit cross-context relations from
  [`SPEC_METHOD.md#bounded-context-semantic-resolution`](SPEC_METHOD.md#bounded-context-semantic-resolution);
- probabilistic construction as a bounded evaluation class from
  [`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#position`](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#position)
  and
  [`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#evaluation`](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#evaluation);
- delegated probabilistic construction, exact candidate production, and
  construction-versus-assessment separation from
  [`SPEC_METHOD.md#agentic-construction-execution-stdo-up-020`](SPEC_METHOD.md#agentic-construction-execution-stdo-up-020);
- governed ambiguity, bounded probabilistic processing, explicit human
  adjudication, and hard-stop separation from
  [`SPEC_METHOD.md#ambiguity-governance-rule`](SPEC_METHOD.md#ambiguity-governance-rule);
- exact-basis evaluation, evidence-and-verdict separation, authority
  conservation, and closed results from
  [`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates`](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates),
  [`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-006-authority-conservation`](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-006-authority-conservation),
  [`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-007-semantic-evidence-and-verdict-separation`](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-007-semantic-evidence-and-verdict-separation),
  and
  [`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-012-closed-results`](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-012-closed-results);
- constitutional derivation and re-entry from
  [`SPEC_METHOD.md#constitutional-chain`](SPEC_METHOD.md#constitutional-chain);
- finite material closure, projection, authority conservation, residual
  uncertainty, and capability fit from
  [`REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#reference-frame-laws`](REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#reference-frame-laws); and
- singular released authority from
  [`SPEC_METHOD.md#one-constitutional-surface-and-version-boundary-stdo-surface-001`](SPEC_METHOD.md#one-constitutional-surface-and-version-boundary-stdo-surface-001).

These references establish provenance. The definitions and laws below are the
sole normative authority for the meaning of `a_c` within the selected complete
STDO cut. A consumer does not need an implicit STDO representation, GTL
carrier, or downstream implementation to interpret the calculus.

This standard introduces the generic calculus identities `F_D`, `F_P`, and
`F_H`. It does not import those identities from an equal-spelled graph,
runtime, ODD, or application shorthand. The predecessor clauses establish the
substrate-neutral evaluation, probabilistic-processing, human-adjudication,
authority, evidence, and refusal principles from which the generic definitions
below are derived. Nominal equality with a predecessor or downstream shorthand
creates no concept-identity, import, or equivalence relation.

The relative links above identify derivation clause families in this authoring
source. Issuance of an exact `AxiomaticCalculusBasis` resolves and records their
absolute predecessor-cut semantic addresses under
`derivation_basis.release_uri`. The mutable authoring links are not themselves
the digest-bound derivation references.

The derivation direction is one-way. A model of STDO under `a_c`, an encoded
carrier, a proof tool, or a successful application cannot amend the source
principles or this calculus.

## Scope

`a_c` governs the form of a symbolic axiomatic model. It answers:

- what identities and typed objects exist;
- how relations bind exact endpoints;
- how constraints, latitude, and residuals remain explicit;
- how traversals and judgments are typed;
- how material closure, projection, overlay, and transformation behave;
- what a model must preserve from its subject; and
- which claims are structural, semantic, or authority decisions.

`a_c` does not choose the subject vocabulary, decide which source declarations
are material, supply semantic acceptance, select a carrier, execute a model, or
prove that one interpretation is uniquely correct.

## Core Signature

An `a_c` signature is:

```text
Sigma = (
  RecordKind,
  Sort,
  RelationKind,
  ConstraintKind,
  ResidualKind,
  FunctorKind,
  JudgmentKind,
  StopKind
)
```

`a_c` fixes this finite core record-kind set:

```text
RecordKind_ac = {
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:semantic-object,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:typed-relation,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:constraint,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:latitude,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:residual,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:traversal,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:transformation,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:judgment
}
```

Every `a_c` signature imports those identities unchanged. A model-family
signature specializes their fields, value domains, reference domains, and
admissible kinds; it does not remove, rename, shadow, or silently add a core
record family. Another fundamental record family requires an explicit
compatible calculus extension rather than an extra subject sort.

Every signature member is a finite, closed identity set for one model family.
The signature defines:

- the fields and value domains of every sort and record family;
- the reference domain and cardinality of every identity-bearing field;
- the allowed source and target sorts for every relation kind;
- the subject and predicate domains of every constraint kind;
- the subject, uncertainty, consequence, and re-entry domains of every
  residual kind;
- the input, output, evidence, and stop contract of every judgment kind; and
- the functor kinds permitted for each traversal.

Unknown kinds and fields are not extensions. They require a new signature or
an explicit compatible extension relation.

An `a_c` model over exact basis `b` is:

```text
M_b = (b, I, O, E, C, L, X, V, T, J)

Population_M = {
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:semantic-object  -> O,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:typed-relation  -> E,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:constraint      -> C,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:latitude        -> L,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:residual        -> X,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:traversal       -> V,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:transformation  -> T,
  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:judgment        -> J
}
```

where:

- `I` is the closed identity universe;
- `O` is the finite set of typed semantic objects;
- `E` is the finite set of typed directed relations;
- `C` is the finite set of constitutional constraints;
- `L` is the finite set of declared latitude records; and
- `X` is the finite set of residual uncertainty records;
- `V` is the finite set of traversal records;
- `T` is the finite set of transformation records; and
- `J` is the finite set of judgment records.

`Population_M` is a total function over `RecordKind_ac`. Every population is
finite, every fundamental record belongs to exactly one population, and record
identities are unique across their disjoint union. Let `Local_M` be that union.
Then `I = Local_M disjoint_union External_M`, where every member of
`External_M` is admitted only through one signature-declared external reference
domain and exact resolution relation. A hidden record, an unpopulated extra
record family, an identity occurring in two populations, or an identity in `I`
with neither one local record nor one lawful external resolution refuses the
model. A population may be empty only when the selected signature does not
require a member of that record kind.

The signature declares a finite reference-domain function:

```text
RefDomain_Sigma(record_kind, field)
  -> (cardinality,
      allowed_local_record_kinds,
      allowed_semantic_object_sorts,
      allowed_external_target_kinds,
      required_basis_relation)
```

Every scalar or collection member that carries an identity reference is
checked through that function. A local reference resolves across the exact
`Population_M` family named by its target record kind; a reference to a
semantic object also satisfies the declared target sort. An external reference
resolves through exactly one declared external target kind and basis relation.
No reference may resolve both locally and externally. Missing field domains,
wrong-family targets, wrong-sort targets, ambiguous targets, and dangling
external identities refuse structural admission.

The tuple is abstract. A carrier may use records, tables, graphs, terms,
clauses, code, or another representation only when its encoding profile proves
that every tuple relation is preserved or explicitly refused.

## Typed Records

The following sections define the exact shapes of the eight core record
families. `SemanticObject`, `TypedRelation`, `Constraint`, `Latitude`, and
`Residual` populate `O`, `E`, `C`, `L`, and `X`. The traversal,
transformation, and judgment records defined below populate `V`, `T`, and `J`.
A traversal, transformation, or judgment is not placed in `O` merely by
reifying its name as a semantic object. A subject model may independently
represent the concept of a record kind, but that representation does not
satisfy the core population law.

### Semantic Object

Every semantic object has exactly:

```text
SemanticObject = {
  id,
  sort,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  value
}
```

`id`, `sort`, `context`, `owner`, and `basis` are identities. `scope` is the
closed governed domain. `value` is sort-defined carrier-neutral content or a
reference to exact content.

### Typed Relation

Every relation has exactly:

```text
TypedRelation = {
  id,
  kind,
  source,
  target,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  qualifiers
}
```

`source` and `target` resolve to members of `I`. `qualifiers` is the closed
kind-specific record declaring direction, cardinality, preservation, loss,
inverse, invalidation, or other relation semantics required by the signature.

### Constraint

Every constraint has exactly:

```text
Constraint = {
  id,
  kind,
  applies_to,
  predicate,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  judgment_kind,
  latitude_ref,
  refusal
}
```

`kind` resolves one declared `ConstraintKind`; `judgment_kind` resolves one
declared `JudgmentKind`. The owning signature defines the predicate language
and how its result is judged. A predicate that is not deterministically
decidable states the required probabilistic or human judgment kind rather than
pretending to be a machine proof.

### Latitude

Latitude is an explicit permission set inside a constraint boundary:

```text
Latitude = {
  id,
  applies_to,
  allowed_variation,
  forbidden_variation,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  invalidation
}
```

Silence is not latitude. Latitude grants no authority beyond its owner, scope,
basis, and invalidation law.

### Residual

Residual uncertainty is first-class model content:

```text
Residual = {
  id,
  subject,
  kind,
  uncertainty,
  consequence,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  re_entry,
  invalidation
}
```

Projection, compression, interpretation, or encoding cannot erase a residual.
It remains represented, is explicitly dispositioned by competent authority, or
causes refusal.

`kind` resolves one declared `ResidualKind`. The owning signature defines its
lawful subject, uncertainty, consequence, re-entry, and invalidation domains.
An undeclared residual kind or value refuses structural admission.

## Fundamental Laws

### AC-001 Closed Signature

Every admitted object, relation, constraint, latitude, residual, traversal,
transformation specialization, and judgment belongs to one declared signature.
Every fundamental record also occurs exactly once in the total
`Population_M` function under its declared `RecordKind_ac`. Missing, duplicate,
shadowed, or unknown record kinds and populations fail closed.

### AC-002 Scoped Identity

An identity resolves one member under one type, context, owner, scope, and
basis. Equal spelling, payload equality, graph position, or carrier equality
does not establish semantic identity.

### AC-003 Reference Closure

Every referenced identity resolves exactly once in the applicable model or
through one explicit external relation. Resolution uses the exact
`RefDomain_Sigma(source_record_kind, field)` declaration across the model's
record populations. Dangling, duplicate, wrong-record-kind, wrong-sort,
wrong-basis, locally-and-externally ambiguous, or undeclared-field references
refuse structural admission.

### AC-004 Relation Typing

A relation is lawful only when its kind admits the exact source and target
sorts and all required qualifiers are present. Direction is material unless the
relation kind explicitly declares symmetry.

### AC-005 Authority Conservation

Objects, relations, constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals,
transformations, projections, and judgments retain their declared semantic,
operation, evaluation, and decision authority. Copying, interpreting, encoding,
evaluating, or transporting a record does not transfer authority.

### AC-006 Basis Coherence

Every fundamental record, model, and result binds an exact basis. Mixed bases
require an explicitly owned composite-basis relation. Individually valid
coordinates do not create a coherent composite basis by proximity.

### AC-007 Constraint And Refusal

Each constraint names its governed subject, predicate, judgment kind,
latitude, and refusal. A failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope, or
invalid-basis result follows the declared result algebra rather than being
coerced to success.

### AC-008 Explicit Latitude

Two values may differ lawfully only through an applicable latitude or
transformation relation. An implementation preference, probabilistic choice,
or human presence is not implicit latitude.

### AC-009 Residual Conservation

Every material uncertainty, omission, translation loss, unresolved boundary,
or unproven relation remains in `X` until an authorized disposition creates an
exact successor model. Absence from a projection is not resolution.

### AC-010 Material Closure

For model `M`, seed set `Z`, and exact dependency relation family `R`, material
closure is the least fixed point:

```text
closure_R(M, Z) = lfp(lambda Q: Z union required_R(M, Q))
```

The result is defined only when `Z`, `R`, required-edge semantics, basis, and
scope are exact and the fixed point is finite and unique. Failure to establish
those conditions returns a gap or refusal. Least closure means least lawful
record closure under `R`; it does not claim globally minimal prose, bytes,
tokens, cost, or cognitive effort.

### AC-011 Projection

A projection selects a view of a model without changing selected meaning:

```text
project(M, Z, R) -> (M_Z, Boundary_Z) | gap | refusal
```

`M_Z` contains the material closure of `Z`. `Boundary_Z` records excluded,
external, unresolved, translated, and invalidation-sensitive seams. A
projection is not a new semantic owner and cannot silently trim a required
member to satisfy a carrier or capability budget.

### AC-012 Overlay

An overlay adds explicit records to one or more declared `Population_M`
families of a basis model. It does not mutate the basis. Override,
disambiguation, equivalence, specialization, or translation exists only as a
typed relation with exact authority, direction, scope, basis, preservation,
loss, refusal, and invalidation semantics.

### AC-013 Transformation

A transformation is an operation-bearing specialization of one exact traversal
record `v`:

```text
t = {
  id,
  traversal,
  domain_model,
  codomain_model,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  operation_authority,
  preconditions,
  preservation_relation,
  preserved,
  introduced,
  removed,
  external_preserved,
  external_introduced,
  external_removed,
  external_resolution_witnesses,
  residuals,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states,
  invalidation,
  re_entry
}
```

`t.traversal` resolves one `v`; its context, owner, scope, basis, operation
authority, evidence, provenance, and stop contract must equal or lawfully
restrict the corresponding traversal coordinates. A broader or mismatched
coordinate refuses.

`domain_model` and `codomain_model` resolve exact content identities of the
complete input and proposed successor models. Each model identity commits to
its exact calculus basis, signature identity, complete finite `Population_M`,
complete `External_M`, exact external-resolution map, and selected
model-content identity under the owning identity law. A mutable locator,
model-family name, partial projection, or population digest without the exact
model identity refuses.

For each `x in External_M`, the model's exact resolution relation determines:

```text
Resolution_M(x) = {
  external_identity,
  reference_domain,
  external_target_kind,
  resolved_target_identity,
  basis_relation,
  resolution_basis,
  evidence_identity
}

ResolutionSet_M = { Resolution_M(x) | x in External_M }
```

`Resolution_M` is a model coordinate supplied by the signature-declared
external reference relation, not a ninth fundamental record family. Every
field is identity-bearing and exact. One external identity has exactly one
resolution tuple in one model; a missing, ambiguous, or extra tuple refuses.

For an ordinary same-basis transformation:

```text
basis(domain_model) = basis(codomain_model) = t.basis = basis(t.traversal)
signature(domain_model) = signature(codomain_model)
```

A cross-basis or cross-signature migration requires a separately identified
transformation specialization whose exact composite-basis and compatible
signature-extension relations name both sides. No identity whose basis or
record kind changes belongs to `preserved`; the source identity is removed and
the successor identity is introduced, with their continuity represented only
by the exact migration relation.

`preservation_relation` resolves one exact typed equality relation applicable
to the declared domain and codomain model identities and record kinds. It binds
both model identities, both exact bases, comparison domain, direction,
authority, scope, evidence, and equality law. Equivalence or
meaning-preservation may relate a removed identity to an introduced identity;
it cannot retain one identity in `preserved`.

Let `Local_b` be the complete input-model local-record identity set, `P_t` the
identities named by `preserved`, `R_t` those named by `removed`, and `N_t` the
identities of the complete records named by `introduced`. A lawful
transformation proves the closed local-record delta:

```text
Local_b       = P_t disjoint_union R_t
Local_b_prime = P_t disjoint_union N_t
N_t intersect Local_b = empty
R_t intersect Local_b_prime = empty
```

For every identity in `P_t`, the input and successor records have the same
record kind, identity, context, owner, scope, and basis. They are either:

1. byte-identical under one exact canonical record grammar selected for both
   models; or
2. equal under the exact `preservation_relation` when the abstract records do
   not share such a byte grammar.

Canonical-byte equality and typed record equality are alternative proofs of
identity preservation, not carrier selection by the calculus. A changed field,
changed basis, changed record kind, nominally equal identifier, equivalence,
or unbound assertion of preserved meaning refuses membership in `P_t`.

Every removed identity is absent from the successor. Every introduced identity
is absent from the input and carries a complete lawful record in exactly one
successor population. Every input local-record identity is classified exactly
once as preserved or removed; no local record may be silently dropped,
retained, or duplicated.

The external-resolution coordinates form a distinct closed delta. Let `E_b`
and `E_b_prime` be `ResolutionSet_M` for the domain and codomain models;
`EP_t`, `ER_t`, and `EN_t` are exactly the resolution coordinates named by
`external_preserved`, `external_removed`, and `external_introduced`:

```text
E_b       = EP_t disjoint_union ER_t
E_b_prime = EP_t disjoint_union EN_t
EN_t intersect E_b = empty
ER_t intersect E_b_prime = empty
```

For every `x in EP_t`, `external_resolution_witnesses` contains exactly one:

```text
ExternalResolutionPreservationWitness = {
  external_resolution: x,
  domain_model,
  codomain_model,
  domain_resolution: Resolution_domain_model(x),
  codomain_resolution: Resolution_codomain_model(x),
  decision: equal,
  evidence
}
```

The two resolution tuples are exactly field-equal. A nominally equal external
identifier, equivalent target, changed target kind, changed resolved target,
changed reference domain, changed basis relation, changed resolution basis, or
missing witness cannot enter `EP_t`. Every member of `ER_t` has its complete
resolution only in the domain model; every member of `EN_t` has its complete
resolution only in the codomain model. A changed external resolution is a
removal followed by introduction of the new resolution coordinate and any
separately declared continuity relation; the referenced external identity may
remain unchanged, but the resolution is not preserved. Witnesses are total and
unique over `EP_t` and name no other resolution coordinate.

Material residuals remain in the successor residual set unless an exact
authorized disposition is included in the transformation evidence. Failure to
establish any model identity, basis, population, local or external partition,
equality, external-resolution witness, residual, or codomain equation refuses.

Application is:

```text
T[t](M_b, inputs) -> M_b_prime* | hold | gap | refusal
```

The exact transformation identity `t` declares every mutation it may perform.
The input model remains unchanged; `M_b_prime*` is a proposed successor. A
proposed successor does not accept or admit itself.

### AC-014 Judgment Separation

A judgment points to an unchanged subject:

```text
Judgment = {
  id,
  kind,
  subject,
  subject_digest,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  evaluator,
  authority,
  decision,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  decided_at
}
```

Issuing a judgment does not transform, rewrite, reissue, or rename its subject.
Promotion is an explicit relation between the unchanged subject and its
admission or acceptance judgment.

## Traversals And Functor Kinds

A traversal is a typed contract:

```text
v = {
  id,
  domain,
  codomain,
  context,
  owner,
  scope,
  basis,
  preconditions,
  postconditions,
  authority,
  evidence,
  provenance,
  stop_states
}
```

`a_c` defines three fundamental functor-kind identities:

```text
F_D = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-d
F_P = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-p
F_H = urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:f-h
```

Application notation is:

```text
F_K[v](X_v) -> Y_v | Omega_v
```

where `F_K` is one functor kind, `v` is one exact traversal identity, `X_v` and
`Y_v` are its typed input and result domains, and `Omega_v` is its closed stop
algebra.

- `F_D` classifies deterministic evaluation or proof over declared properties.
  It returns a judgment and does not perform the domain construction being
  judged.
- `F_P` classifies bounded probabilistic interpretation, construction, or
  proposal under an exact traversal contract. Its result has no semantic,
  admission, acceptance, or closure authority merely because it is useful or
  repeatable.
- `F_H` classifies explicit human adjudication under an exact identity,
  authority grant, subject, basis, and decision contract. Human presence grants
  no ambient authority.

The actor, executor, domain operation, and functor kind are different
coordinates. `Encode`, `Interpret`, `Serialize`, `Measure`, and other named
domain operations are not aliases for `F_D`, `F_P`, or `F_H`. Different
traversals may share one functor kind without sharing identity, semantics,
inputs, outputs, authority, or evidence.

`Functor Kind` is an `a_c` term for this traversal classification. It does not
by itself assert a category-theoretic functor. A model claiming categorical
functor laws additionally defines its source and target categories and proves
identity and composition preservation.

### AC-015 Functor Classification

Every functor application binds exactly one functor kind and one traversal
identity. Applying any `F_*` kind without bracketed traversal identity `[v]` is
incomplete.

### AC-016 Typed Composition

Two traversals compose only when the first result type and judgment satisfy the
second traversal's exact domain and preconditions:

```text
F_K2[w] compose F_K1[v]
```

Composition retains both traversal identities, intermediate results,
judgments, evidence, authority, provenance, and stop states. It cannot flatten
probabilistic proposal, deterministic evaluation, and human decision into one
undifferentiated operation. `a_c` prescribes no universal `F_P -> F_D -> F_H`
sequence; each application owns its lawful topology.

## Interpretation And Models

An interpretation applies `a_c` to an exact subject:

```text
Interpret_a_c(subject_basis, signature, interpretation_contract)
  -> M_subject* | hold | gap | refusal
```

The trailing `*` marks a proposed model that has not received the applicable
semantic acceptance judgment.

The interpretation contract declares:

- exact `a_c` basis;
- exact subject identity, inventory, and bytes or semantic addresses;
- selected signature and any compatible extension relation;
- mapping from subject declarations to every applicable model record population,
  including objects, relations, constraints, latitude, residuals, traversals,
  transformations, and judgments;
- interpreter identity, capability, provenance, and stop states;
- structural evaluation contract;
- semantic selection and acceptance authority; and
- source re-entry and invalidation rules.

The proposed model `M_subject*` does not become accepted through construction.
Structural evaluation can prove closed shape, reference typing, identity
derivation, and basis coherence. It cannot prove that probabilistic semantic
selection retained every material subject meaning. Semantic acceptance remains
a separately recorded authority judgment.

### AC-017 Interpretation Fidelity

Every admitted model record maps to exact subject provenance or is explicitly
identified as model-local content under competent authority. Every evaluated
subject declaration has a retained, omitted, residual, inapplicable, or refused
disposition. Interpretation cannot treat absence as immateriality without a
recorded basis and authority.

### AC-018 Structural And Semantic Separation

Structural conformance decides closed syntax, types, identities, references,
bases, and mechanically decidable predicates. Semantic fidelity decides the
meaning and materiality of the interpretation. Structural success is evidence
for semantic review, not a substitute for it.

### AC-019 Valid Model

A model `M_b` is a valid model of `a_c` under signature `Sigma`, written:

```text
M_b satisfies a_c[Sigma]
```

only when:

1. `Sigma` and the exact `a_c` basis resolve;
2. every record satisfies AC-001 through AC-009;
3. every claimed closure, projection, overlay, transformation, judgment, and
   composition satisfies its applicable law;
4. interpretation fidelity and residual dispositions bind the exact subject;
5. structural evaluation and semantic acceptance remain distinct and both
   required where claimed; and
6. all evidence, provenance, invalidation, and re-entry coordinates resolve.

A checker may decide the structural subset. No generic checker may claim the
semantic or authority subset unless the model supplies an exact lawful decision
contract for it.

## Subject And Carrier Boundaries

The three governed layers are:

```text
a_c       = the pure calculus
a_c.X     = subject X interpreted as a model of a_c
a_c.X.C   = that accepted model encoded in carrier C
```

Their relations are:

```text
M_X = Interpret_a_c(X)
J_X = Accept_X(M_X) -> accepted | refuse
G_C = Encode_C(M_X, J_X) where J_X = accepted
D_C = F_D[v_carrier_admission](G_C, Profile_C, CarrierBasis_C)
      -> admitted | refuse
```

`J_X` is an external semantic-acceptance judgment over unchanged `M_X`.
Encoding requires `J_X.decision = accepted` and exact equality between the
judgment subject identity and digest and `M_X`; hold or refusal cannot be
encoded. `D_C` is a judgment over unchanged carrier bytes. It is not a
transformed carrier. The admitted encoding evidence relation is the exact
triple `(G_C, J_X, D_C)`; neither judgment enters the identity of its subject.

### AC-020 Layer And Release Separation

`a_c`, `a_c.X`, and `a_c.X.C` have independent content identities, judgments,
supersession relations, and proof obligations:

- `a_c` qualification evaluates internal coherence against its complete
  declared calculus-law set;
- `a_c.X` proves faithful interpretation of exact subject `X`; and
- `a_c.X.C` proves faithful, canonical encoding of the accepted model in
  carrier `C`.

An encoding failure does not change `a_c.X`. An interpretation failure does not
change `a_c`. A downstream success cannot ratify an upstream layer or basis.
None of these layers is automatically an independently released Product. The
external authority that selects and releases one owns that Product status.

## Exact Calculus Identity

The stable concept identity does not identify one immutable calculus edition.
An exact released calculus basis is an external record created after the
publication bytes exist. It keeps the predecessor authority from which the
edition was derived distinct from the successor carrier that publishes it:

```text
AxiomaticCalculusBasis = {
  kind: "stdo.axiomatic-calculus-basis",
  schema_version: 1,
  concept_identity: "urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c",
  derivation_basis: {
    release_uri: absolute immutable predecessor release URI,
    manifest_sha256: "sha256:" + 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters,
    principle_refs: non-empty absolute semantic-address URI[]
  },
  publication_basis: {
    release_uri: absolute immutable successor release URI,
    manifest_sha256: "sha256:" + 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters,
    member_uri: absolute URI for this member in that release,
    member_sha256: "sha256:" + 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters
  }
}
```

The record uses RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme bytes. Duplicate object
names are rejected before canonicalization. `derivation_basis.principle_refs`
is duplicate-free and sorted by ascending unsigned UTF-16 code units. Its
identity is:

```text
urn:stdo:axiomatic-calculus-basis:sha256:
  + sha256(JCS(AxiomaticCalculusBasis))
```

`derivation_basis` binds one exact accepted predecessor cut and the complete
finite set of clauses from which this edition was derived. Every principle
reference is one clause identified under `Derivation Provenance`, resolves
inside that predecessor cut, and is retained without a hard-coded member count.
The set is recomputed when the derivation account changes. It cannot depend on
the publication carrier or calculus-basis identity being created.

`publication_basis` binds the distinct immutable successor carrier and this
standard's exact bytes. Its member URI resolves inside its release URI. The
record is external because this standard cannot contain its own final byte
digest. Same-release references that cite this calculus are publication or
cross-context relations, not derivation provenance.

An interpreted-subject identity binds at least:

```text
id(a_c.X) binds
  exact id(a_c)
  + exact subject basis id(X)
  + exact interpretation contract
  + selected model content identity
  + semantic-selection ledger identity and digest
```

An external semantic-acceptance judgment points to that unchanged identity and
content digest. It is not embedded in `id(a_c.X)`. The accepted interpretation
is the pair `(a_c.X, J_X)` where `J_X` is the applicable accepted judgment. This
one-way relation prevents the acceptance record and its subject from requiring
each other's final identity.

An encoded-carrier identity binds at least:

```text
id(a_c.X.C) binds
  exact id(a_c.X)
  + exact carrier Product or cut
  + exact encoding profile
  + canonical carrier content identity
```

The accepted semantic judgment remains external to both content identities.
Encoding mechanically verifies its subject identity and digest against the
unchanged interpreted model and retains it in the evidence relation. The
carrier-admission judgment points to the unchanged carrier identity and digest
and is not embedded in `id(a_c.X.C)`. The admitted encoding relation is the
triple `(a_c.X.C, J_X, D_C)`. Any Product acceptance and release likewise point
to the unchanged content-first layer identity rather than entering it.

The owning Product defines the canonical record grammar and issuance authority
for those downstream identities. It cannot omit the upstream identities or
replace them with mutable locators.

## Application Boundary

This standard defines the generic relations `a_c.X` and `a_c.X.C`. It selects,
constructs, accepts, or releases no concrete interpretation or carrier. A
downstream authority owns its exact subject population, interpretation,
carrier, judgments, and Product or release status. The downstream identity is
never embedded back into the calculus or its publication basis.

## External Imports And Specializations

An application may declare a typed import, translation, or specialization of
an `a_c` concept under that application's own exact authority, context, basis,
scope, preservation, loss, refusal, and invalidation law. Such a relation is
external to the calculus. It neither changes `a_c` nor enters this standard by
being useful to an application.

## Exclusions

`a_c` is not:

- a representation or compression of its derivation source;
- a selected semantic model of any subject;
- a carrier profile or carrier instance;
- an executable language, interpreter, compiler implementation, or runtime;
- a deterministic semantic assessor or theorem prover;
- a required graph storage topology;
- a world-model ontology;
- an authority registry; or
- a claim that all governed systems share one vocabulary or relation set.

## Conformance Obligations

Review and qualification of this fundamental standard cover at least:

1. closed signature, `RecordKind_ac`, population, field, value-domain, and
   reference-domain definitions;
2. well-typed positive and refusal examples for every fundamental law;
3. identity uniqueness and cross-context collision cases;
4. closure, projection, overlay, transformation, and composition laws,
   including exact model identities, population partitions, basis equality,
   and byte-or-typed-equality preservation refusal;
5. strict separation of domain operations, functor kinds, actors, and
   judgments;
6. residual and authority conservation through interpretation and encoding;
7. exact calculus-basis identity reconstruction;
8. direct-coordinate, cross-family reference, wrong-family, duplicate-family,
   and dangling-reference refusal cases for every fundamental record family;
9. derivation-basis and publication-basis reconstruction with cyclic and
   same-carrier counterexamples; and
10. one neutral toy model demonstrating that the calculus has no hidden
    derivation-source record, application-profile, or carrier dependency.

No example, checker, model, or carrier can qualify a law outside the exact
claim it evaluates.

1	# Ticket Method
2	
3	## Core Model
4	
5	### Goals
6	
7	The Product Definition Overlay's `ticketing.goals` binding locates the current
8	epic layer. `GOALS.md` is the default file.
9	
10	Goals are:
11	
12	- broader than one ticket
13	- narrower and more current than `INTENT.md`
14	- the place to state the active work wave and what matters now
15	
16	Goals are not the durable unit of execution tracking.
17	
18	### Tickets
19	
20	Tickets are the enduring work records.
21	
22	Each ticket is:
23	
24	- one durable record; one markdown file is the default carrier
25	- the source of truth for that unit of work
26	- durable across sessions
27	- typed, so bugs and features share one system
28	
29	Tickets are used when work needs independent durable identity for:
30	
31	- feature work
32	- bug tracking
33	- spikes
34	- chores
35	
36	### Sprints
37	
38	Sprints are bounded execution batches.
39	
40	Each sprint is:
41	
42	- one manifest under the Product Definition Overlay's optional
43	  `ticketing.sprints.root`; `.ai-workspace/sprints/` is the default
44	- a control surface for a bounded body of work
45	- a place to batch repeated authority references, closure law, evidence
46	  expectations, and deferred local compliance debt
47	- closed by an explicit sprint-close review
48	
49	Sprints are not constitutional authority. They operate under `SPEC_METHOD.md`
50	and the project surfaces they cite.
51	
52	A sprint may contain durable tickets, manifest-local iteration entries, or both.
53	Use tickets for work items that need durable identity across sessions. Use
54	manifest-local iteration entries for small changes whose only independent value
55	is traceability inside the sprint.
56	
57	The sprint is the batch authority. It does not erase the need for paydown
58	tickets when close review finds debt that must survive past the sprint.
59	
60	### Comments
61	
62	The Product Definition Overlay's `ticketing.comments.root` is the message
63	board.
64	`.ai-workspace/comments/` is the default binding.
65	
66	Comments are for:
67	
68	- publishing ideas
69	- strategy notes
70	- reviews
71	- handoffs
72	- closure summaries
73	- decisions and reasoning
74	
75	Comments are not task status authority. The publication rules for comments are
76	governed by `POSTING_GUIDE.md`.
77	
78	### Execution Contracts
79	
80	Tickets are durable work authority.
81	
82	Execution contracts are the run-scoped admitted work surface derived from a
83	ticket, from a sprint manifest plus included ticket or iteration entry, or
84	drafted during intake when no durable or sprint-local work identity is required.
85	
86	The important distinction is:
87	
88	- a ticket survives sessions and work waves
89	- a sprint survives one bounded execution batch and its close review
90	- an execution contract is the current admitted execution function for one run
91	
92	Execution contracts are not a rival backlog or a second planning surface.
93	
94	They exist so the system can:
95	
96	- classify the work before execution
97	- admit or reject the drafted classification against deterministic criteria
98	- log the admitted execution basis into runtime/event truth
99	- assemble prompts from admitted work law instead of from raw user phrasing
100	- evaluate closure against the same admitted criteria
101	
102	So the intended loop is:
103	
104	1. work arrives
105	2. the system selects the smallest lawful work carrier for its required lifetime
106	3. an agent drafts one run-scoped execution contract from that carrier
107	4. the system validates and admits or rejects the contract
108	5. execution may proceed in the same invocation under the admitted contract
109	6. closure is checked against that same contract
110	7. resulting state still flows through normal proof, gap analysis, and repricing
111	
112	### Milestone And Phase-Scoped Truth (`STDO-UP-006`)
113	
114	A ticket may contain several closure-bearing milestones without becoming
115	several tickets. Each milestone has stable identity, a bounded claim, relevant
116	dependencies, current state, required evidence, and an explicit relation to
117	ticket closure.
118	
119	Milestone acceptance proves only its declared claim. Accepted design does not
120	satisfy implementation, installed proof, qualification, or release. Ticket
121	completion requires every closure-bearing milestone to be accepted; optional
122	or deferred work requires an explicit disposition and owner. Commentary and
123	generated summaries cannot mutate milestone or ticket truth.
124	
125	---
126	
127	## Default Layout
128	
129	```text
130	stdo_default.json
131	
132	specification/
133	├── GOALS.md
134	
135	.ai-workspace/
136	├── sprints/
137	├── tickets/
138	│   ├── backlog/
139	│   ├── active/
140	│   └── completed/
141	└── comments/
142	    └── <agent-id>/
143	```
144	
145	The applicable Product Definition resolves `POSTING_GUIDE.md` and
146	`TICKET_METHOD.md` from its exact shared installed STDO basis. Their absence
147	from the project tree is not absence from the governing method.
148	
149	This is the starter file layout. A conforming `stdo_<label>.json` definition
150	may bind the same ticket, comment, and sprint roles to existing directories,
151	repository resources, tracker collections, API endpoints, or product-scoped
152	queries without restructuring the project.
153	
154	---
155	
156	## Authority
157	
158	- `ticketing.goals` locates the epic layer
159	- `ticketing.sprints.root`, when present, is the bounded execution-batch and
160	  sprint-close review layer
161	- `ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog`, `.active`, and `.completed` locate the
162	  ticket authority
163	- `ticketing.comments.root` locates the discussion and publication layer
164	
165	The paths shown in the default layout are the bindings supplied by
166	`stdo_default.json`. The definition locates these carriers but does not own
167	their ticket or comment content.
168	
169	There is no separate mandatory `ACTIVE_TASKS.md` in this model.
170	
171	If a project later wants a board view, it may generate one from the bound
172	ticket authority. That board is a projection only and must not become the
173	source of truth unless the Product Definition Overlay explicitly rebinds the
174	ticket authority to that carrier and no rival remains.
175	
176	---
177	
178	## Sprint Rules
179	
180	### One Durable Record Per Sprint
181	
182	Each sprint has one durable manifest record. The default carrier is one
183	markdown file. Another bound carrier must preserve the same identity, required
184	fields, history, closure law, and one-truth relation.
185	
186	Recommended local-file naming:
187	
188	- `SPRINT-2026-04-30-process-navigator.md`
189	- `SPRINT-2026-05-12-dashboard-density.md`
190	
191	For a local file, the filename should carry:
192	
193	- stable id
194	- short slug
195	
196	### Sprint Manifest Required Fields
197	
198	Each sprint manifest must record at least:
199	
200	- `id`
201	- `title`
202	- `status`
203	- `goal`
204	- `opened_at`
205	- `updated_at`
206	- `authority_refs`
207	- `scope`
208	- `excluded_boundaries`
209	- `expected_change_classes`
210	- `included_tickets` or `iterations`
211	- `closure_trigger`
212	- `closure_law`
213	- `proof_surface`
214	- `deferred_compliance`
215	- `non_closure_conditions`
216	- `paydown_policy`
217	
218	`authority_refs` names the upstream Goals, Intent, Product, Requirement,
219	Design, or other governing surfaces the sprint operates under.
220	
221	`excluded_boundaries` names what the sprint is not allowed to change. Typical
222	exclusions include product truth, data contracts, runtime semantics,
223	governance/closure law, public carrier shape, and release criteria.
224	
225	`deferred_compliance` names any local proof, review, accessibility, screenshot,
226	walkthrough, test, design wording, or trace cleanup intentionally deferred until
227	sprint close.
228	
229	`paydown_policy` states how deferred debt becomes accepted, ticketed, repriced,
230	or removed during close review.
231	
232	### Sprint Status
233	
234	Minimum sprint status model:
235	
236	- `active`
237	- `closing`
238	- `closed`
239	- `superseded`
240	
241	The intended meaning is:
242	
243	- `active`: iteration is admitted inside the sprint boundary
244	- `closing`: new iteration is frozen while close review and paydown
245	  classification run
246	- `closed`: close review finished and all remaining debt is accepted, ticketed,
247	  repriced, or removed
248	- `superseded`: the sprint boundary was wrong and a new authority surface,
249	  sprint, or ticket set replaced it
250	
251	Projects may add `planned` or `cancelled` if needed, but those states do not
252	replace close review.
253	
254	### Sprint Admission
255	
256	A sprint may admit work only when the manifest makes the boundary reviewable.
257	
258	Admission requires:
259	
260	- a bounded scope
261	- cited authority
262	- expected change classes
263	- explicit excluded boundaries
264	- a closure law
265	- non-closure conditions
266	- a paydown policy for deferred compliance
267	
268	The sprint may batch repeated closure criteria that would otherwise be copied
269	into every included ticket.
270	
271	The sprint may not batch away intake triage. Substantive included tickets still
272	record their lawful `change_class` and `re_entry_point`. Manifest-local
273	iteration entries may rely on the sprint's declared class only when they remain
274	inside the sprint scope and excluded boundaries.
275	
276	### Sprint Compliance Escrow
277	
278	A sprint may defer local compliance proof only when:
279	
280	- the manifest names the deferred proof or cleanup class
281	- the debt is local to the sprint's admitted surface
282	- expected correction cost is lower than per-change proof cost
283	- the sprint is short enough that the debt remains reviewable
284	- the close review must classify and pay down the debt
285	
286	Deferred compliance is not silent debt. It is escrow held by the sprint.
287	
288	The following may be eligible for escrow when the governing method allows it:
289	
290	- screenshots or walkthrough capture
291	- visual review
292	- accessibility cleanup
293	- replay proof for product-meaningful UX interactions
294	- design wording cleanup
295	- trace cleanup
296	- local realization cleanup
297	
298	The following may not be hidden in escrow:
299	
300	- new product truth
301	- new or changed data contracts
302	- new runtime, governance, closure, provenance, or evidence semantics
303	- missing constructive carriers
304	- changed public graph functions or AssetSurface contracts
305	- law-changing work that needs `goal_reprice`, `intent_reprice`,
306	  `product_reprice`, `requirement_reprice`, or `design_reframe`
307	
308	If one of those appears during the sprint, the sprint records the finding and
309	the work exits the sprint path through a standalone ticket, a repricing action,
310	or sprint supersession.
311	
312	### Sprint Close Review
313	
314	Sprint close begins by moving the manifest to `status: closing`.
315	
316	While closing:
317	
318	- new iteration inside that sprint is frozen
319	- every included ticket or iteration entry is reviewed against the manifest
320	- accumulated evidence is checked for durability
321	- changed surfaces are walked against cited authority
322	- deferred compliance is classified
323	- paydown tickets are opened where debt must survive past the close review
324	
325	Each reviewed item is classified as one of:
326	
327	- `accepted`: compliant under the sprint authority
328	- `local_paydown`: local debt remains and is captured by a paydown ticket
329	- `design_reframe`: the work needs design repricing
330	- `requirement_reprice`: the work needs requirement repricing
331	- `product_reprice`: the work changes product definition
332	- `remove`: the work should be backed out or kept out of closure
333	
334	A sprint may move to `closed` only when every item and every debt entry is
335	classified and the resulting paydown or repricing work is durable.
336	
337	Sprint close can accept local paydown debt only when the governing method allows
338	that debt to survive as explicit follow-up. Sprint close cannot accept hidden
339	authority drift.
340	
341	---
342	
343	## Ticket Rules
344	
345	### One Durable Record Per Ticket
346	
347	Each ticket has one durable authoritative record. The default carrier is one
348	markdown file. A repository or external tracker carrier is lawful only when it
349	preserves the required ticket contract, history, state transition, stable
350	identity, searchability, and closure semantics without a co-equal local copy.
351	
352	Recommended local-file naming:
353	
354	- `T-001-add-product-layer.md`
355	- `B-002-fix-reset-manifest-id.md`
356	- `S-003-evaluate-integration-capability.md`
357	- `C-004-clean-up-trace-tags.md`
358	
359	For a local file, the filename should carry:
360	
361	- stable id
362	- short slug
363	
364	### Multi-Build-Tenant Ticket Independence
365	
366	This clause consumes the build-tenancy bounded context
367	`urn:stdo:bounded-context:build-tenancy` declared by
368	`SPEC_METHOD.md#what-how-and-work-carriers`. `TICKET_METHOD.md` owns the
369	multi-build-tenant work-item and ticket-lifecycle relation inside that context;
370	it does not redefine build-tenant identity or realization meaning.
371	
372	A **Multi-Build-Tenant Work Item** is one admitted upstream work item with more
373	than one build-tenant execution line. The upstream authority and each
374	tenant-local ticket retain distinct identities and lifecycles.
375	
376	If one source/product/design work item must be realized in more than one build
377	tenant, do not track all tenant realizations inside one ticket lifecycle.
378	
379	This rule governs:
380	
381	- backlog tickets
382	- active tickets
383	
384	It is not retroactive for historical completed tickets unless a completed
385	ticket is reopened or explicitly repriced.
386	
387	This does **not** mean every ticket becomes multi-tenant.
388	
389	Use tenant duplication only when the same admitted work item genuinely has more
390	than one tenant execution line.
391	
392	So there are three lawful cases:
393	
394	1. upstream-only ticket
395	   - source/product/design authority only
396	   - no tenant duplicate yet
397	2. single-tenant ticket
398	   - one tenant-local execution line only
399	   - no sibling tenant duplicate required
400	3. multi-tenant work item
401	   - one upstream authority ticket
402	   - one suffixed tenant-local ticket per tenant execution line
403	
404	Instead:
405	
406	- keep the upstream source/product/design ticket as its own authority surface
407	- duplicate the work item into one tenant-local ticket per build tenant
408	- append a build-tenant mnemonic to the base ticket id and filename
409	- keep status, proof, closure, and reopen logic independent for each tenant
410	
411	Recommended examples:
412	
413	- source/product ticket: `B-030-publish-capability-profile...`
414	- first tenant ticket: `B-030-T1-publish-capability-profile...`
415	- second tenant ticket: `B-030-T2-publish-capability-profile...`
416	
417	The important law is:
418	
419	- one ticket must not claim closure for more than one build-tenant lifecycle
420	- a tenant-local blocker or false closure in one tenant must not be hidden by
421	  green status in another tenant
422	- tenant-local proof, repricing, and reopening remain tenant-local
423	
424	If a tenant-local duplicate exists, it should record:
425	
426	- `source_ticket`
427	- `build_tenant`
428	
429	The `build_tenant` value must identify the applicable entry in the product's
430	`how.build_tenants` definition. A path name, display alias, or tracker label
431	does not replace that tenant identity unless the Product Definition Overlay
432	binds it as the identity.
433	
434	The unsuffixed/base ticket may remain the upstream product or design authority.
435	
436	If the work item is multi-tenant, tenant execution and closure for
437	backlog/active work must live on the suffixed duplicates.
438	
439	If the work item is single-tenant, no sibling duplicate is required.
440	
441	### Required Fields
442	
443	Each ticket must record at least:
444	
445	- `id`
446	- `title`
447	- `type`
448	- `ticket_category`
449	- `status`
450	- `goal`
451	- `change_intent`
452	- `change_class`
453	- `re_entry_point`
454	- `triaged_at`
455	- `created_at`
456	- `updated_at`
457	
458	Recommended additional fields:
459	
460	- `priority`
461	- `dependencies`
462	- `links`
463	- `intake_source`
464	- `affected_boundary`
465	- `source_ticket` when this ticket duplicates or derives from another ticket
466	- `build_tenant` when this ticket is tenant-local
467	
468	For `ticket_category: implementation_migration`, also require:
469	
470	- `migration_strategy`
471	- `library_usage`
472	
473	For tenant-local implementation migrations, also require:
474	
475	- `build_tenant`
476	- `source_ticket` when the tenant-local ticket duplicates or derives from an
477	  upstream source/product/design ticket
478	
479	For `ticket_category: implementation_migration`, also conditionally require:
480	
481	- `governing_library` when `library_usage: consume` or `library_usage: extend`
482	- `library_rationale` when `library_usage: none`
483	
484	For execution-contract admission, the runtime-drafted contract should also
485	carry, at minimum:
486	
487	- `target_truth`
488	- `superseded_truth` when relevant
489	- `closure_law`
490	- `evaluation_criteria`
491	- `non_closure_conditions`
492	- `proof_surface`
493	
494	### Allowed Types
495	
496	Minimum common set:
497	
498	- `feature`
499	- `bug`
500	- `spike`
501	- `chore`
502	
503	Projects may add more, but this default set should be enough for most cases.
504	
505	### Ticket Category
506	
507	Ticket category is orthogonal to ticket type.
508	
509	- ticket type answers: what kind of work record is this?
510	- ticket category answers: what execution discipline or migration discipline
511	  governs the ticket?
512	
513	Minimum common set:
514	
515	- `ordinary`
516	- `implementation_migration`
517	
518	This means a `feature`, `bug`, `spike`, or `chore` may all carry:
519	
520	- `ticket_category: ordinary`
521	- `ticket_category: implementation_migration`
522	
523	Use `implementation_migration` when the ticket is not just “change code until
524	tests pass”, but a governed replacement of one implementation truth path with
525	another across producers, consumers, projections, and proof surfaces.
526	
527	Typical examples:
528	
529	- a bug ticket that must replace an old tracker/read-model family with one new
530	  authoritative carrier
531	- a feature ticket that introduces a new public interface and requires all
532	  producers/consumers to migrate to it before closure
533	- a refactor ticket that removes a bridge path or compatibility facade from an
534	  authoritative contract family
535	
536	### Inside-Out First Ticket Sequencing
537	
538	For `ticket_category: implementation_migration`, ticket sequencing must reflect
539	the inside-out rule from `SPEC_METHOD.md`.
540	
541	That means:
542	
543	- tickets that publish or admit the new authoritative source carrier are the
544	  upstream tickets in the wave
545	- tickets that harden prompt assembly, projections, reports, dossiers, review
546	  surfaces, or other downstream consumers must depend on those upstream source
547	  tickets
548	- downstream tickets may carry exploratory work while the source ticket is
549	  active, but that work is non-closure evidence until the source carrier is
550	  admitted and authoritative
551	- a downstream ticket must not close while its upstream source-carrier ticket
552	  remains open
553	
554	In practice, if one migration wave introduces:
555	
556	- a new source carrier
557	- then prompt/projection/read-model consumers of that carrier
558	
559	the ticket dependency chain must run:
560	
561	`source carrier -> downstream consumers`
562	
563	not the reverse.
564	
565	### Change Class
566	
567	Ticket type and change class are orthogonal.
568	
569	- ticket type answers: what kind of work record is this?
570	- change class answers: where does this change lawfully re-enter the
571	  constitutional chain?
572	
573	Tickets must record the `change_class` declared by intake triage, using the
574	change classes from `SPEC_METHOD.md`.
575	
576	Common pairings are:
577	
578	- `feature` with `goal_reprice`, `intent_reprice`, `product_reprice`,
579	  `requirement_reprice`, or `design_reframe`
580	- `bug` with `requirement_reprice`, `design_reframe`, or
581	  `realization_refactor`
582	- `chore` with `design_reframe` or `realization_refactor`
583	- `spike` as exploratory work that still carries the current triage class and
584	  should terminate either in a more specific downstream ticket or in an
585	  explicit decision that no further substantive change is required
586	
587	Ticket category and change class are also orthogonal.
588	
589	- `change_class` governs lawful constitutional re-entry
590	- `ticket_category` governs ticket execution and closure discipline
591	
592	So a ticket may be:
593	
594	- `type: bug`
595	- `ticket_category: implementation_migration`
596	- `change_class: design_reframe`
597	
598	without contradiction.

600	### Upward Propagation Check
601	
602	Triage consumes `SPEC_METHOD.md#computed-classification-and-treatment` for the
603	declared owner/layer traversal, complete relevant Public membership and value
604	delta, accepted-design scope and trace coverage, and rule-determined treatment.
605	The owning work carrier references that exact result and its residuals; a new
606	role does not repeat an unchanged walk.
607	
608	Before declaring `realization_refactor` for a bug, establish that the current
609	requirement and accepted realizing design govern the affected behavior and
610	remain sufficient for the authorized outcome. Their mere presence proves no
611	coverage. Missing or ambiguous evidence leaves the affected treatment unknown;
612	it is not proof that the governing layer itself is absent.
613	
614	If the governing requirement is actually missing or insufficient, re-enter its
615	owner; if that requirement is sufficient but the realizing design is missing or
616	insufficient, re-enter Design. Follow any actual upstream Goal, Intent or
617	Product change to its owner rather than stopping at a familiar file. When the
618	current requirement and accepted design suffice and implementation deviates,
619	repair or reject the candidate under `realization_refactor`. A candidate's
620	Public violation does not select a new contract. An explicitly changed desired
621	outcome or established governing insufficiency follows the owning re-entry;
622	unresolved meaning remains J and reserved choice O.

625	
626	Because tickets are the durable authority surface for work tracking, a ticket
627	for substantive work must carry the minimum metadata required by
628	`SPEC_METHOD.md` intake triage.
629	
630	That means the ticket must record at least:
631	
632	- the declared `change_intent`
633	- the lawful `change_class`
634	- the lawful `re_entry_point`

637	### Work-Carrier-To-Execution Rule
638	
639	Every execution governed by this method uses one run-scoped execution contract.
640	The required lifetime of the work or obligation selects the smallest lawful
641	source carrier. First establish applicable upstream work authority, then select
642	the first matching row. For work inside an admitted sprint, the local carrier
643	boundary is that sprint; otherwise it is the current run.
644	
645	| Condition | Execution-contract source | Durable-ticket decision |
646	|---|---|---|
647	| no applicable upstream work authority exists | no execution contract is admitted | do not create a ticket as substitute authority; stop or re-enter |
648	| applicable authority exists and an existing admitted ticket covers the exact work | derive the run-scoped contract from that ticket | reuse it; do not create another ticket |
649	| applicable authority exists, no exact admitted ticket covers the work, and work or an open obligation needs independent state beyond the local carrier boundary | use one durable ticket plus the run-scoped contract | create or update the ticket only under ticket-state authority |
650	| applicable authority exists, no exact admitted ticket covers the work, and work stays inside one admitted sprint with no state required after sprint close | use the sprint manifest plus one manifest-local iteration entry | do not create a durable ticket |
651	| applicable authority exists, no exact admitted ticket or sprint covers the work, and work ends in the current run with no independent surviving state | use an intake-drafted run-scoped contract | do not create a durable ticket |
652	
653	`Ticket-shaped` describes the categorization, closure criteria, proof surface,
654	non-closure conditions, and other required execution-contract fields. It does
655	not create durable ticket identity or ticket-lane state.
656	
657	Absence of a durable ticket neither requires nor authorizes creating one. An
658	exact Product-authorized work instruction may supply upstream work authority
659	for a one-run contract; a generic request or model-widened scope cannot. Create
660	or update a durable ticket only when the table requires surviving state and the
661	actor holds ticket-state authority.
662	
663	An explicit instruction from ticket-state authority to create a durable record
664	selects that durability. It does not admit an execution contract or widen its
665	upstream work authority.
666	
667	The system may draft, validate, admit, and execute a contract in one invocation.
668	Drafting and admission remain distinct relations within that invocation; no
669	separate turn, ticket, or approval ceremony is implied. Execution begins only
670	after deterministic admission or explicit human override of the exact contract.
671	The drafting model must not infer admission from its own draft, ticket or sprint
672	presence, lane placement, or `active` status.
673	
674	The admitted result identifies the Product-bound admission mechanism and
675	authority, exact contract identity or digest, decision, and evidence, including
676	any exact human override. If those coordinates are absent, the contract remains
677	drafted or rejected; prose asserting `admitted` is not admission evidence.
678	
679	The admitted contract also names one Product-bound durable result/evidence
680	surface. Every execution result, withheld closure, and residual obligation is
681	recorded there before return. A conversation return alone is not durable
682	evidence. If no such surface is authorized and available, contract admission
683	refuses.
684	
685	Absent or rejected admission returns the missing work authority without
686	execution. Before return, an obligation that must survive the run becomes a
687	sprint-local entry when its lifetime remains inside the admitted sprint;
688	otherwise it is recorded as a durable ticket only under ticket-state authority.
689	If that authority is absent, retain the obligation in the contract's named
690	durable result/evidence surface or an already-authorized enclosing carrier,
691	mark closure withheld on ticket-state authority, and return the required
692	re-entry.
693	
694	Execution and closure use the same admitted categorization, criteria, proof
695	surface, and non-closure conditions. Resulting state still flows through proof,
696	gap analysis, and repricing.
697	
698	### Execution Contract Admission
699	
700	The runtime execution flow should treat the ticket, sprint entry, or drafted
701	work contract as an admission candidate, not as automatic truth.
702	
703	Minimum expected states are:
704	
705	- `drafted`
706	- `admitted`
707	- `rejected`
708	- `superseded`
709	
710	An admitted execution contract should be:
711	
712	- logged in runtime/event truth
713	- available to prompt assembly
714	- available to later closure checking
715	
716	The system must not allow the model to silently self-certify its own execution
717	basis without deterministic admission or explicit human override.
718	
719	Execution-contract admission validates a proposed contract against its cited
720	Product outcome, prerequisite, or experiment basis; it does not admit that
721	growth basis. Admission or renewal of the basis belongs to the authority owning
722	the selected Goals work wave, or its explicitly bounded proxy, and remains
723	durably legible in existing Goals or ticket authority. Drafting, admitting, or
724	retaining an active execution contract cannot create or renew authority that
725	the owning work-wave authority has not admitted.
726	
727	### Execution And Verification Authority Separation (`STDO-UP-007`)
728	
729	Authority to author or implement a change is not independent authority to
730	verify it. Where independent review is required, the reviewer is not the author
731	of the reviewed subject and identifies the exact subject, basis, scope,
732	exclusions, evidence, verdict, and unresolved findings.
733	
734	Self-review remains useful authoring evidence but cannot be relabeled as
735	independent. Human authority may accept or reject the claim; it does not make
736	implementer self-review independent. Independent review is required at Product,
737	qualification, release, and explicitly risk-bearing boundaries that claim it,
738	not for every local implementation step.
739	
740	A claimed independent review may support promotion or closure only when its
741	exact subject and verdict are durably traceable through an existing ticket,
742	commentary, qualification, or release-evidence carrier. A statement that review
743	occurred, an unbound conversation summary, or an unavailable draft is not the
744	review verdict. This rule requires no separate receipt, carrier, or review
745	round.
746	
747	A review verdict is bounded by the exact reviewed claim and its applicable hard
748	stops. A finding blocks current promotion only when it falsifies that claim,
749	exposes competing or ambiguous authority on its acceptance path, violates
750	applicable active authority, safety, or retained accepted behavior, or
751	establishes a material architectural decision with durable consequences that
752	forecloses an admitted Product outcome.
753	
754	A valid observation outside that boundary is repricing input. It does not by
755	itself widen the reviewed subject, block its bounded claim, or require a new
756	ticket, artifact, review round, or implementation increment.
757	
758	A direct or lawfully proxied human ruling receives durable disposition before
759	the next affected acceptance boundary. Its source wording remains distinct
760	from agent interpretation. Opening a ticket records the obligation but does not
761	satisfy it, and an agent cannot widen the ruling while recording it.
762	
763	Where `SPEC_METHOD.md`'s Agentic Construction Execution relation applies, the
764	active work item identifies the selected execution basis, bounded affected
765	relation set, delegated construction and assessment authority, and re-entry
766	conditions. It may point to accepted design and existing evidence carriers
767	rather than restating them. Ticket state, ticket prose, or an admitted execution
768	contract cannot widen that basis or substitute for the live-surface assessment
769	required by the protocol.
770	
771	The reviewable transition may be carried by an existing ticket, commentary,
772	commit, qualification, or release-evidence surface. No new ticket state,
773	document type, review round, or approval ceremony is required. Ticket Method
774	carries selection and traceability; `SPEC_METHOD.md` owns the execution
775	semantics.
776	
777	### Recorded Judgment And Owner-Ruling Continuity
778	
779	A residual judgment needed by another activation is recorded once with its
780	owning work in the existing carrier selected by Work-Carrier-To-Execution Rule.
781	It identifies the question, exact subject and governing basis, supporting
782	computed facts/evidence, responsible actor and authority, conclusion and
783	scope, uncertainty, and a concrete revising observation. That observation must
784	let a consumer determine whether the conclusion still applies. A rule-settled
785	question needs no invented J record.
786	
787	Later roles and resumed runs recover the result and check applicability rather
788	than re-author unchanged judgment. Changed material evidence, basis or the
789	stated revising observation causes affected reassessment, preserving the
790	original result and its successor relation. Retain unrelated conclusions only
791	where their independence from the change is supported. A new role or
792	conversation alone is not an invalidator. The result may reference current C
793	outputs; reuse cannot silently turn unknown facts into established premises.
794	
795	Required independent assessment may consume valid C, but its assessor acquires
796	sufficient exact evidence and supplies its own judgment under the actual
797	independence condition. Reusing the author's J cannot satisfy that condition.
798	
799	Record a direct or lawfully proxied owner ruling in its original wording, with
800	its owner, exact subject/basis, permitted scope and effects, conditions and
801	source, separately from agent interpretation. Later work consumes that same
802	ruling while applicable; it neither widens it nor requests unchanged authority
803	again. New ambiguity or a materially changed decision returns only the affected
804	question to its owner. J is not O, and recording either cannot create admission,
805	acceptance, effects or continuation beyond the original grant.
806	
807	These results follow the existing run, sprint or durable-ticket lifetime and
808	named result/evidence surface. They require no separate judgment registry,
809	ticket per judgment, or additional approval ceremony.
810	
811	### Bounded-Context Term Binding
812	
813	Ticket and work-instruction terms resolve under `SPEC_METHOD.md`'s
814	Bounded-Context Semantic Resolution law. A ticket may use an unqualified term
815	when its cited Product, re-entry surface, execution basis, and affected scope
816	select exactly one bounded-context meaning.
817	
818	When a ticket spans contexts or a material term has competing meanings, the
819	ticket cites the applicable Product Definition Overlay disambiguation or the
820	owner-authorized import, translation, equivalence, or disambiguation carrier.
821	It may reference that relation rather than duplicate it. Ticket prose, actor
822	familiarity, a matching glossary heading, tenant placement, or comment context
823	cannot select meaning or transfer authority.
824	
825	An unresolved or multiply resolved material term blocks execution-contract
826	admission and closure for the affected claim. Opening or updating the ticket
827	records the pressure but does not cure it; resolution re-enters at the authority
828	that owns the missing context or semantic relation.

830	### Evaluation Criteria And Non-Closure Conditions
831	
832	Execution contracts should expose both:
833	
834	- what counts as progress or completion
835	- what still counts as failure even if some local proof is green
836	
837	At minimum, the contract should make visible:
838	
839	- `evaluation_criteria`
840	- `non_closure_conditions`
841	
842	These are the local gain function for the work.
843	
844	For implementation migrations, typical non-closure conditions include:
845	
846	- old authoritative path still passes in normal execution within the declared
847	  affected scope
848	- mixed old/new proof is still accepted
849	- proxy or partial interface implementation still stands in the acceptance path
850	- competing or ambiguous executable authority remains reachable on the claimed
851	  Product acceptance path
852	- ticket wording, product wording, and proof wording are not reconciled
853	
854	These conditions are not optional commentary. They are the anti-self-deception
855	surface for execution.
856	
857	Residual implementation debt outside the claimed acceptance path is not a
858	non-closure condition by itself. It may be deferred only under the
859	path-relative authority and explicit disposition rules in `SPEC_METHOD.md`.
860	
861	### Condition-Based Closure And Reuse
862	
863	A work claim is complete only when every applicable declared obligation is
864	satisfied by valid evidence for its exact subject, basis and scope, all required
865	judgments and owner rulings are present and applicable, and no active
866	non-closure condition remains. A mandatory but unknown applicability or
867	insufficient-evidence result withholds the dependent claim; evidence presence
868	alone is not satisfaction. The existing owner decides any reserved acceptance.
869	
870	Review evaluates these conditions; its occurrence is not the closing event.
871	Where applicable law requires no independent review or reserved acceptance,
872	the authorized Writer may record the satisfied bounded result in the existing
873	carrier without adding a ticket, Executive appointment, review or design-view
874	recreation solely to mark completion. This does not waive a condition that
875	actually applies, including sprint-close or design-method law.
876	
877	An unchanged obligation reuses valid applicable evidence and recorded J/O.
878	A material counterexample, changed evidence or basis invalidates the affected
879	claim and its dependent results before further reliance. An unrelated
880	observation is retained as bounded repricing input; it does not reopen a
881	satisfied claim or expand work automatically. Closure recording preserves the
882	exact evaluated scope, satisfied conditions, evidence and remaining residuals.
883	
884	### Test Case Authority
885	
886	Tests are proof projections from admitted work authority.
887	
888	Every substantive test case should derive from:
889	
890	```text
891	ticket -> intake triage -> lawful re-entry point -> governing requirement,
892	design, module, graph, carrier, or closure surface -> test expectation
893	```
894	
895	Tests do not derive authority from the current implementation.
896	
897	Implementation behavior is evidence. It is not the arbiter of the expected
898	result when code and tests disagree.
899	
900	When a ticket is fixed and a mismatch appears between implementation behavior
901	and test expectation, review must reconcile the mismatch in this order:
902	
903	1. the ticket's `change_intent`, `change_class`, `re_entry_point`,
904	   `target_truth`, `superseded_truth`, `closure_law`,
905	   `evaluation_criteria`, and `non_closure_conditions`
906	2. the ticket's intake triage and lawful owning re-entry
907	3. the governing requirement, design, module, graph-function, carrier, or
908	   other cited authority surface
909	4. the test case expectation
910	5. the implementation
911	
912	The implementation may prove that a test is stale, incomplete, or too narrow,
913	but it cannot by itself authorize changing the expected result.
914	
915	Changing a test only because the current code behaves differently is a
916	ticket-method defect.
917	
918	If a test predates a lawful ticket repricing, update or remove the test only
919	after naming the governing ticket and the authority change that superseded the
920	old expectation.
921	
922	If the ticket is stale, ambiguous, or missing the authority needed to decide the
923	test expectation, the work must re-enter triage before either the code or test
924	is treated as correct.
925	
926	A passing test is closure evidence only when the test expectation can be traced
927	back to the admitted ticket and its governing authority chain.
