929	### Implementation Migration Category
930	
931	If `ticket_category: implementation_migration`, the ticket must carry both:
932	
933	1. an explicit migration declaration block
934	2. a hard migration checklist
935	
936	This is not optional commentary. It is part of the ticket authority.
937	
938	`SPEC_METHOD.md` defines the migration law. This ticket category defines the
939	minimum ticket-local declaration and checklist that a reviewer can check before
940	accepting a closure claim on one concrete work item.
941	
942	The ticket must explicitly declare:
943	
944	- the migration strategy used for this work item
945	- the exact affected migration scope
946	- every explicitly excluded or disjoint Product or compatibility scope and its
947	  deterministic routing relation
948	- the old truth path or superseded contract
949	- the new truth path or authoritative contract
950	- the producer set for the old and new path
951	- the consumer set for the old and new path
952	- every projection, report, status surface, and proof surface derived from that
953	  contract family
954	- the closure law for the migration
955	
956	At minimum, the ticket must carry this checklist in live markdown form:
957	
958	```md
959	## Migration Checklist
960	
961	- [ ] exact affected migration scope is named
962	- [ ] excluded or disjoint Product and compatibility scopes are named with deterministic routing
963	- [ ] old truth path is named explicitly
964	- [ ] new truth path is named explicitly
965	- [ ] producer set for the new truth is listed
966	- [ ] consumer set for the new truth is listed
967	- [ ] projection/read-model surfaces are listed
968	- [ ] old truth path is removed or explicitly demoted from authority within the affected scope
969	- [ ] mixed-state behavior is no longer accepted as closure evidence
970	- [ ] tests proving mixed old/new behavior are removed or repriced
971	- [ ] recurring realization patterns are checked against existing library/commonization surfaces
972	- [ ] ticket declares library usage and names the governing library or rationale
973	- [ ] if the work exists in more than one build tenant, this backlog/active ticket carries only one tenant lifecycle and any sibling tenant work lives on its own suffixed ticket
974	- [ ] ticket wording, product wording, and proof claims are reconciled before closure
975	```
976	
977	This ticket category is the local ticket-method enforcement surface for the
978	inside-out migration law defined in `SPEC_METHOD.md`.
979	
980	The required field is:
981	
982	- `migration_strategy`
983	- `library_usage`
984	
985	Allowed values are:
986	
987	- `inside_out_hard_break`
988	- `fundamental_re_adoption`
989	
990	Allowed `library_usage` values are:
991	
992	- `none`
993	- `consume`
994	- `extend`
995	
996	If `library_usage: consume` or `library_usage: extend`, the ticket must name
997	the governing reusable library/commonization surface in `governing_library`.
998	
999	If `library_usage: none`, the ticket must explain in `library_rationale` why:
1000	
1001	- no existing reusable surface applies, or
1002	- the pattern is still boundary-specific, or
1003	- this is not yet a lawful recurrence/commonization candidate
1004	
1005	For `ticket_category: implementation_migration`, closure is blocked while the
1006	old authoritative interface still passes in normal execution within the
1007	declared affected scope unless the ticket explicitly declares a retained
1008	compatibility feature. A deterministically routed, non-overlapping Product scope
1009	outside the declared affected scope remains governed by its own current
1010	authority.
1011	
1012	That means:
1013	
1014	- the old path may not remain silently authoritative within the affected scope
1015	- mixed old/new green tests do not count as migration completion
1016	- any retained old path within the affected scope must be named as
1017	  compatibility rather than current native truth
1018	- retained compatibility must be justified in the ticket itself rather than
1019	  inferred from surviving code
1020	- proxy or partial implementations do not satisfy migration closure
1021	- if a ticket was marked `completed` and later review shows checked closure
1022	  items are false on the current tree, the ticket must be reopened or an
1023	  explicitly linked successor ticket must be created; a false closure claim is
1024	  a ticket-method defect, not just a code defect
1025	
1026	An intermediate Product-slice milestone inside an open implementation-migration
1027	ticket may be accepted under the path-relative promotion rule in
1028	`SPEC_METHOD.md`. Its identity and acceptance criteria must derive from Product
1029	plus every causally applicable live requirement, accepted design relation, and
1030	retained predecessor claim; ticket wording cannot narrow that authority away.
1031	The ticket remains active and must not claim migration closure until the
1032	migration checklist and final closure law are satisfied.
1033	
1034	Active ticket status does not renew the accepted slice's exhausted growth
1035	authority. Work that only discharges already admitted removal, demotion, and
1036	migration-closure proof obligations may continue within their existing bound
1037	without claiming further Product progress. Further material producer or
1038	consumer growth requires another still-live basis admitted under
1039	`STDO-UP-013`; ticket activity alone is not that basis.

1041	### Migration Strategy Requirements
1042	
1043	If `migration_strategy: inside_out_hard_break`, the ticket must carry:
1044	
1045	- a full best-guess interface inventory for the migrating contract family
1046	- the ordered break sequence from deepest source truth outward
1047	- the old seam each break intentionally severs
1048	- the negative proof expected for each break
1049	
1050	If `migration_strategy: fundamental_re_adoption`, the ticket must carry:
1051	
1052	- the explicit human Product-authority selection of fundamental re-adoption
1053	- the comparison with bounded evolution across Product value, feedback latency,
1054	  authority risk, reversibility, total cost, and retained predecessor semantics
1055	- the bounded abort or re-entry condition
1056	- the sideways reference line or prior implementation boundary being treated as
1057	  source material
1058	- the module and interface adjudication surface
1059	- explicit classifications for inherited modules, interfaces, carriers,
1060	  projections, and proof surfaces
1061	
1062	Allowed inherited-implementation classifications are:
1063	
1064	- `carry_across`
1065	- `redundant`
1066	- `rewrite`
1067	
1068	Unclassified inherited implementation blocks closure.

1070	### Recurring Realization And Library Declaration
1071	
1072	Implementation migration tickets must declare whether the active boundary is:
1073	
1074	- rebuilding a pattern locally
1075	- consuming an existing reusable library/commonization surface
1076	- extending that surface before the local implementation lands
1077	
1078	This is what `library_usage` records.
1079	
1080	The recurrence rule is:
1081	
1082	- the second credible recurrence forces an explicit library/commonization review
1083	- the third local rebuild is not acceptable by default
1084	
1085	If review shows the same realization pattern already exists in two module
1086	boundaries or tickets, a third local rebuild blocks implementation unless the
1087	ticket does one of these:
1088	
1089	- declares `library_usage: consume`
1090	- declares `library_usage: extend`
1091	- links an explicit do-not-commonize design decision in `library_rationale`
1092	
1093	Preferred order is:
1094	
1095	1. boundary-local cleanup
1096	2. tenant-local reusable library/commonization surface
1097	3. shared/common propagation only through separate design re-entry
1098	
1099	If a reusable pattern is discovered during the active ticket, the second- and
1100	third-recurrence rules above still apply. Outside those rules and the current
1101	claim's applicable hard stops, the pattern is repricing input. It does not block
1102	the bounded claim or require a follow-up ticket unless the owning authority
1103	admits that follow-up.

1105	### Multi-Build-Tenant Review Rule
1106	
1107	If the same work item is being processed across multiple build tenants, review
1108	of backlog/active tickets must check that:
1109	
1110	1. each tenant has its own suffixed ticket
1111	2. each ticket names its `build_tenant`
1112	3. each tenant ticket has its own proof surface and closure law
1113	4. one tenant's green proof does not stand in for another tenant's closure
1114	5. reopen, repricing, and successor work remain tenant-local unless the
1115	   upstream source/product/design ticket itself must be changed
1116	
1117	### Implementation Migration Review Disambiguation
1118	
1119	Implementation migration tickets must make the review problem concrete enough
1120	that an implementor cannot land a rename, adapter, wrapper, or happy-path proof
1121	and claim source-truth migration.
1122	
1123	For a core-interface or carrier migration, the ticket should include a
1124	`Functional Review Criteria` section. The criteria must be specific to the
1125	ticket, but reviewers should be able to answer these generic questions:
1126	
1127	1. Did the change replace control-flow-owned meaning with carrier-owned,
1128	   algebra-owned, event-owned, or otherwise admitted source truth?
1129	2. Did the change reduce or remove a semantic center, or only rename and
1130	   relocate it behind helpers?
1131	3. Is the new law expressed as a typed/closed carrier, contract, or transition
1132	   family rather than an open dict, string protocol, or config-shaped surface?
1133	4. Is the main step readable as a pure transform over admitted truth, or does it
1134	   still contain orchestration that decides the law procedurally?
1135	5. Are effects pushed to the edge, such as event emission, manifest
1136	   publication, file/output publication, or operator delivery, instead of being
1137	   mixed into source-truth interpretation?
1138	6. Do downstream consumers pattern-match or otherwise consume the admitted
1139	   carrier directly, or do they reconstruct truth from payloads, `.get(...)`,
1140	   fallback defaults, raw text, or legacy files?
1141	7. Are projections and reports derived from event/source truth, or can they
1142	   still close independently as a second authority surface?
1143	8. If deterministic gates, validation, or F_D-like checks exist, do they inform
1144	   the current state without structurally blocking the lawful constructive or
1145	   F_P-like path that the admitted contract permits?
1146	9. If the same realization pattern already exists elsewhere, does the ticket
1147	   explicitly consume or extend a reusable library/commonization surface rather
1148	   than rebuilding it locally again?
1149	
1150	Passing tests do not satisfy this section by themselves. A slice that keeps the
1151	same semantic center alive behind typed wrappers, adapter-local policy, old
1152	lists beside new algebra, fallback config, or rehydrated dict payloads still
1153	fails migration review even if public behavior remains green.
1154	
1155	### Impacted Interface Review Checklist
1156	
1157	For a core-interface, carrier, or authoritative-contract migration, the ticket
1158	must include an `Impacted Interface Review Checklist` before tests can be used
1159	as closure evidence.
1160	
1161	This checklist is a named walk of every live interface that can still bypass,
1162	reinterpret, replay, or project the migrating truth path.
1163	
1164	At minimum it should enumerate, when they exist:
1165	
1166	- the source-carrier builder
1167	- closure/register/projection builders
1168	- deepest semantic kernel and adapter boundaries
1169	- public wrappers, bootstrap, replay, ingest, resume, and query entrypoints
1170	- prompt/report/projection/read-model surfaces
1171	- constructor/materialization paths
1172	- proof lanes and negative-proof fixtures
1173	
1174	Each checklist item must state what counts as closure for that interface.
1175	
1176	Examples:
1177	
1178	- “`<conformance-module>::consume_projection` consumes the admitted carrier or
1179	  projection and does not import raw helper authority”
1180	- “`<query-module>::project_domain` exposes a read model only and does not
1181	  silently rebuild the carrier when publication is absent”
1182	- “`<gap-module>::build_canonical_gap` does not aggregate open payload rows into
1183	  an independent closure decision”
1184	
1185	Review rules:
1186	
1187	- a checked box asserts truth on the current tree, not merely intended
1188	  direction
1189	- if review shows a checked interface item is false, the ticket is not
1190	  closure-ready
1191	- if an interface is intentionally deferred, the ticket must name the successor
1192	  ticket or leave that item unchecked
1193	- compatibility shims do not satisfy the checklist unless they are explicitly
1194	  justified as retained compatibility
1195	- for `inside_out_hard_break`, the checklist must describe the seam inventory
1196	  before tests are used as closure evidence
1197	- for `fundamental_re_adoption`, the checklist must cover inherited modules and
1198	  interfaces being carried, dropped, or rewritten; implicit carry-forward does
1199	  not count
1200	
1201	### Required Break Order And Break-To-Closure Map
1202	
1203	Implementation migration tickets that touch a core interface must include a
1204	`Required Break Order` or equivalent ordered execution section.
1205	
1206	The order must start at the authoritative source carrier and move outward:
1207	
1208	1. discover the full best-guess interface family
1209	2. publish or admit the new source carrier
1210	3. deliberately sever one old authoritative seam and keep it broken
1211	4. rebind the deepest semantic kernel to that carrier
1212	5. remove or demote old producers
1213	6. rebind old consumers
1214	7. reprice projections, reports, prompts, delivery bindings, and tests
1215	
1216	The ticket must also include a `Break-To-Closure Map` when the migration has
1217	multiple old interfaces. The map must state which break closes which
1218	closure-law clause. Without that map, partial landing can look like full
1219	landing.
1220	
1221	Reviewers must treat the following as explicit defects:
1222	
1223	- a typed wrapper that still carries old semantic authority
1224	- a new carrier added beside the old authoritative read model
1225	- a proxy or partial implementation that keeps the old interface alive behind a
1226	  new name
1227	- constructor, replay, ingest, resume, bootstrap, or public-wrapper paths that
1228	  bypass admission
1229	- a projection or test that can pass without the new carrier
1230	- a fallback path that invents missing policy, identity, target, or closure
1231	  truth
1232	- a downstream proof that passes while upstream source-carrier work remains open
1233	
1234	### Mixed-State Negative Proof
1235	
1236	For a migration ticket, positive behavior proof is not enough.
1237	
1238	The proof surface should include at least one negative or structural proof that
1239	the old path can no longer satisfy the closure law. Examples include:
1240	
1241	- the severed seam in the current break is rejected before downstream repair is
1242	  accepted as progress
1243	- removing the new carrier makes advancement, closure, prompt assembly, or
1244	  projection fail closed rather than silently falling back
1245	- a legacy payload without the admitted carrier is rejected instead of
1246	  rehydrated into current truth
1247	- old and new truth intentionally disagree in a fixture and the new truth wins
1248	  or the run fails closed
1249	- a same-name carrier, graph function, route, policy, or projection source with
1250	  different structure fails closed instead of being accepted as equivalent
1251	- required closure proof does not depend on undeclared local fixtures or mutable
1252	  sibling workspaces
1253	
1254	If the old path still works in normal execution within the declared affected
1255	scope, or remains reachable on the claimed acceptance path, the ticket remains
1256	open unless that path is explicitly specified as retained compatibility. A
1257	deterministically routed, non-overlapping Product scope outside the declared
1258	affected scope remains governed by its own current authority and does not block
1259	the migration merely because its path still works.
1260	
1261	For tickets with an `Impacted Interface Review Checklist`, the negative proof
1262	must exercise the named public consumers that matter for closure. Proving that
1263	one legacy shim is bypassed is not sufficient when the live authority path
1264	already bypasses that shim through other helpers, loaders, or rebuild paths.
1265	
1266	### Allowed Status
1267	
1268	Minimum status model:
1269	
1270	- `backlog`
1271	- `active`
1272	- `completed`
1273	
1274	Projects may add `blocked`, `cancelled`, or other explicit local states later
1275	if needed, but the base method starts with `backlog`, `active`, and
1276	`completed`.
1277	
1278	### Ticket Lanes
1279	
1280	Backlog tickets live at the Product Definition Overlay's
1281	`ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog` binding. The default is:
1282	
1283	- `.ai-workspace/tickets/backlog/`
1284	
1285	Active tickets live at `ticketing.tickets.lanes.active`. The default is:
1286	
1287	- `.ai-workspace/tickets/active/`
1288	
1289	Completed tickets move to `ticketing.tickets.lanes.completed`. The default is:
1290	
1291	- `.ai-workspace/tickets/completed/`
1292	
1293	The intended meaning is:
1294	
1295	- `backlog`: accepted durable work that should remain visible but is not part
1296	  of the current execution focus
1297	- `active`: the current bounded execution set
1298	- `completed`: closed work retained as history
1299	
1300	This keeps the live execution set small enough that `rg` remains fast and
1301	readable without forcing deferred work into comments or goals.
1302	
1303	### One-Truth State Projection And Drift Refusal (`STDO-UP-009`)
1304	
1305	Work state has one authority chain: Goals own the bounded work wave, the ticket
1306	owns ticket state, milestone authority owns subordinate milestone state, and
1307	accepted design owns realization decisions. Comments, dashboards, registers,
1308	indexes, and generated summaries are projections.
1309	
1310	Recency, visibility, or repetition does not turn a projection into truth.
1311	Contradiction between the owning ticket, required milestones, current Goals, or
1312	cited acceptance evidence blocks closure. Superseded evidence remains history
1313	and cannot be projected as current acceptance.
1314	
1315	---
1316	
1317	## Recommended Ticket Shape
1318	
1319	Recommended sprint shape:
1320	
1321	```md
1322	# SPRINT-2026-04-30 Operational Projection UX Iteration
1323	
1324	- id: SPRINT-2026-04-30-operational-projection
1325	- status: active
1326	- goal: operational-projection-ux
1327	- opened_at: 2026-04-30T09:00:00Z
1328	- updated_at: 2026-04-30T09:00:00Z
1329	
1330	## Authority
1331	
1332	- specification/GOALS.md#operational-projection-ux
1333	- specification/PRODUCT.md#operational-projection
1334	- <governing-design-surface>/OPERATIONAL_PROJECTION.md
1335	
1336	## Scope
1337	
1338	Iterate an operational projection surface for layout, readability,
1339	interaction affordance, and visual evidence quality.
1340	
1341	## Excluded Boundaries
1342	
1343	- no product truth changes
1344	- no data contract changes
1345	- no runtime or governance semantics changes
1346	- no new constructive carrier
1347	
1348	## Expected Change Classes
1349	
1350	- realization_refactor
1351	
1352	## Iterations
1353	
1354	- id: UXI-001
1355	  intent: improve relation-line readability
1356	  evidence_ref: screenshots/2026-04-30/UXI-001.png
1357	  debt: accessibility contrast check pending
1358	
1359	## Closure
1360	
1361	- closure_trigger: timebox, changed surface volume, or design-lead close request
1362	- closure_law: forensic walkthrough reviews each changed state against authority
1363	- proof_surface: screenshots plus walkthrough notes
1364	- deferred_compliance: screenshots, accessibility check, event-replay review
1365	- non_closure_conditions: product truth or data contract drift remains hidden
1366	- paydown_policy: open paydown tickets for accepted local debt; reprice authority drift
1367	```
1368	
1369	```md
1370	# T-001 Add Product Layer To SPEC_METHOD
1371	
1372	- id: T-001
1373	- type: feature
1374	- ticket_category: ordinary
1375	- status: active
1376	- goal: methodology-bootstrap
1377	- change_intent: make the product-definition layer explicit in the constitutional chain
1378	- change_class: product_reprice
1379	- re_entry_point: product
1380	- triaged_at: 2026-04-07
1381	- priority: high
1382	- created_at: 2026-04-07
1383	- updated_at: 2026-04-07
1384	
1385	## Context
1386	
1387	`SPEC_METHOD.md` included intent and requirements flow but omitted the explicit
1388	product-definition layer.
1389	
1390	## Acceptance
1391	
1392	- `PRODUCT.md` is part of the constitutional chain
1393	- bootstrap sequence includes `intent -> product -> requirements`
1394	- examples and reconstruction logic reflect the new layer
1395	
1396	## Links
1397	
1398	- comment: `.ai-workspace/comments/<agent-id>/...`
1399	```
1400	
1401	For an implementation migration ticket:
1402	
1403	```md
1404	# B-010 Replace Mixed Gap Projection With One Authoritative Carrier
1405	
1406	- id: B-010
1407	- type: bug
1408	- ticket_category: implementation_migration
1409	- migration_strategy: inside_out_hard_break
1410	- library_usage: none
1411	- library_rationale: this migration is boundary-specific and does not establish a recurring realization pattern
1412	- status: active
1413	- goal: operator-gap-truth
1414	- change_intent: replace the mixed operator gap truth with one authoritative declared carrier
1415	- change_class: design_reframe
1416	- re_entry_point: design_surface
1417	- triaged_at: 2026-04-20
1418	- created_at: 2026-04-20
1419	- updated_at: 2026-04-20
1420	
1421	## Migration Declaration
1422	
1423	- affected_scope: gap projection on the declared operator-query acceptance path
1424	- excluded_or_disjoint_scopes: none
1425	- old_truth_path: fallback gap projection with synthetic convergence fields
1426	- new_truth_path: explicit declared-obligation projection plus separately classified fallback gaps
1427	- producers_old: `<gap-module>::build_fallback_gap`
1428	- producers_new: `<obligation-module>::collect_declared_obligations`, `<gap-module>::build_canonical_gap`
1429	- consumers_old: `<query-module>::project_gaps`, `<summary-module>::project_span`, `<review-surface>::render`
1430	- consumers_new: `<query-module>::project_gaps`, `<summary-module>::project_span`, `<review-surface>::render`
1431	- derived_surfaces:
1432	  - `<query-surface>::gaps`
1433	  - `<summary-surface>::span`
1434	  - `<proof-surface>::first_slice_negative`
1435	- closure_law: migration closes only when the old projection is no longer authoritative within the affected scope and mixed old/new proof does not count as acceptance
1436	
1437	## Migration Checklist
1438	
1439	- [ ] exact affected migration scope is named
1440	- [ ] excluded or disjoint Product and compatibility scopes are named with deterministic routing, or explicitly declared absent
1441	- [ ] old truth path is named explicitly
1442	- [ ] new truth path is named explicitly
1443	- [ ] producer set for the new truth is listed
1444	- [ ] consumer set for the new truth is listed
1445	- [ ] projection/read-model surfaces are listed
1446	- [ ] old truth path is removed or explicitly demoted from authority within the affected scope
1447	- [ ] mixed-state behavior is no longer accepted as closure evidence
1448	- [ ] tests proving mixed old/new behavior are removed or repriced
1449	- [ ] recurring realization patterns are checked against existing library/commonization surfaces
1450	- [ ] ticket declares library usage and names the governing library or rationale
1451	- [ ] if the work exists in more than one build tenant, this backlog/active ticket carries only one tenant lifecycle and any sibling tenant work lives on its own suffixed ticket
1452	- [ ] ticket wording, product wording, and proof claims are reconciled before closure
1453	```
1454	
1455	---
1456	
1457	## Operating Mode
1458	
1459	The default local-file carrier assumes:
1460	
1461	- humans and agents can read the active ticket folder directly
1462	- backlog remains searchable durable work, but does not compete with the active
1463	  lane for immediate attention
1464	- `rg` is sufficient for finding active work
1465	- no database or board is required
1466	
1467	Typical commands for that default carrier:
1468	
1469	```bash
1470	rg -n "^#|^- status:|^- type:|^- goal:" .ai-workspace/tickets/active
1471	rg -n "^#|^- status:|^- type:|^- goal:" .ai-workspace/tickets/backlog
1472	rg -n "T-001|B-002" .ai-workspace/tickets
1473	```
1474	
1475	---
1476	
1477	## Relationship To Other Surfaces
1478	
1479	- `GOALS.md` answers: what broad work wave matters now
1480	- `SPEC_METHOD.md` answers: what constitutional change class and re-entry point
1481	  govern the work
1482	- sprints answer: what bounded execution batch is currently pricing proof,
1483	  evidence, and paydown
1484	- tickets answer: what durable units of work exist and what state they are in
1485	- comments answer: what was proposed, argued, decided, reviewed, or handed off
1486	- `POSTING_GUIDE.md` answers: how comment-layer publications are structured and
1487	  named
1488	
1489	This separation prevents:
1490	
1491	- goals becoming an overloaded backlog
1492	- active work being diluted by every deferred ticket
1493	- comments becoming informal task status
1494	- task boards becoming accidental authority
1495	
1496	---
1497	
1498	## Future Extensions
1499	
1500	This minimal method can later grow into:
1501	
1502	- a generated active board
1503	- ticket dependency checks
1504	- links from tickets to scenario, requirement, or ADR surfaces
1505	- external sync with a real ticketing system
1506	- message-board integration through a standard tool-protocol capability
1507	
1508	The durable local-file model remains the default and must remain valid when
1509	selected. Another carrier is not required to reproduce its folders, but it must
1510	preserve the same ticket authority and refusal laws.
1511

# Ticket Method

## Core Model

### Goals

The Product Definition Overlay's `ticketing.goals` binding locates the current
epic layer. `GOALS.md` is the default file.

Goals are:

- broader than one ticket
- narrower and more current than `INTENT.md`
- the place to state the active work wave and what matters now

Goals are not the durable unit of execution tracking.

### Tickets

Tickets are the enduring work records.

Each ticket is:

- one durable record; one markdown file is the default carrier
- the source of truth for that unit of work
- durable across sessions
- typed, so bugs and features share one system

Tickets are used when work needs independent durable identity for:

- feature work
- bug tracking
- spikes
- chores

### Sprints

Sprints are bounded execution batches.

Each sprint is:

- one manifest under the Product Definition Overlay's optional
  `ticketing.sprints.root`; `.ai-workspace/sprints/` is the default
- a control surface for a bounded body of work
- a place to batch repeated authority references, closure law, evidence
  expectations, and deferred local compliance debt
- closed by an explicit sprint-close review

Sprints are not constitutional authority. They operate under `SPEC_METHOD.md`
and the project surfaces they cite.

A sprint may contain durable tickets, manifest-local iteration entries, or both.
Use tickets for work items that need durable identity across sessions. Use
manifest-local iteration entries for small changes whose only independent value
is traceability inside the sprint.

The sprint is the batch authority. It does not erase the need for paydown
tickets when close review finds debt that must survive past the sprint.

### Comments

The Product Definition Overlay's `ticketing.comments.root` is the message
board.
`.ai-workspace/comments/` is the default binding.

Comments are for:

- publishing ideas
- strategy notes
- reviews
- handoffs
- closure summaries
- decisions and reasoning

Comments are not task status authority. The publication rules for comments are
governed by `POSTING_GUIDE.md`.

### Execution Contracts

Tickets are durable work authority.

Execution contracts are the run-scoped admitted work surface derived from a
ticket, from a sprint manifest plus included ticket or iteration entry, or
drafted during intake when no durable or sprint-local work identity is required.

The important distinction is:

- a ticket survives sessions and work waves
- a sprint survives one bounded execution batch and its close review
- an execution contract is the current admitted execution function for one run

Execution contracts are not a rival backlog or a second planning surface.

They exist so the system can:

- classify the work before execution
- admit or reject the drafted classification against deterministic criteria
- log the admitted execution basis into runtime/event truth
- assemble prompts from admitted work law instead of from raw user phrasing
- evaluate closure against the same admitted criteria

So the intended loop is:

1. work arrives
2. the system selects the smallest lawful work carrier for its required lifetime
3. an agent drafts one run-scoped execution contract from that carrier
4. the system validates and admits or rejects the contract
5. execution may proceed in the same invocation under the admitted contract
6. closure is checked against that same contract
7. resulting state still flows through normal proof, gap analysis, and repricing

### Milestone And Phase-Scoped Truth (`STDO-UP-006`)

A ticket may contain several closure-bearing milestones without becoming
several tickets. Each milestone has stable identity, a bounded claim, relevant
dependencies, current state, required evidence, and an explicit relation to
ticket closure.

Milestone acceptance proves only its declared claim. Accepted design does not
satisfy implementation, installed proof, qualification, or release. Ticket
completion requires every closure-bearing milestone to be accepted; optional
or deferred work requires an explicit disposition and owner. Commentary and
generated summaries cannot mutate milestone or ticket truth.

---

## Default Layout

```text
stdo_default.json

specification/
├── GOALS.md

.ai-workspace/
├── sprints/
├── tickets/
│   ├── backlog/
│   ├── active/
│   └── completed/
└── comments/
    └── <agent-id>/
```

The applicable Product Definition resolves `POSTING_GUIDE.md` and
`TICKET_METHOD.md` from its exact shared installed STDO basis. Their absence
from the project tree is not absence from the governing method.

This is the starter file layout. A conforming `stdo_<label>.json` definition
may bind the same ticket, comment, and sprint roles to existing directories,
repository resources, tracker collections, API endpoints, or product-scoped
queries without restructuring the project.

---

## Authority

- `ticketing.goals` locates the epic layer
- `ticketing.sprints.root`, when present, is the bounded execution-batch and
  sprint-close review layer
- `ticketing.tickets.lanes.backlog`, `.active`, and `.completed` locate the
  ticket authority
- `ticketing.comments.root` locates the discussion and publication layer

The paths shown in the default layout are the bindings supplied by
`stdo_default.json`. The definition locates these carriers but does not own
their ticket or comment content.

There is no separate mandatory `ACTIVE_TASKS.md` in this model.

If a project later wants a board view, it may generate one from the bound
ticket authority. That board is a projection only and must not become the
source of truth unless the Product Definition Overlay explicitly rebinds the
ticket authority to that carrier and no rival remains.

---

## Sprint Rules

### One Durable Record Per Sprint

Each sprint has one durable manifest record. The default carrier is one
markdown file. Another bound carrier must preserve the same identity, required
fields, history, closure law, and one-truth relation.

Recommended local-file naming:

- `SPRINT-2026-04-30-process-navigator.md`
- `SPRINT-2026-05-12-dashboard-density.md`

For a local file, the filename should carry:

- stable id
- short slug

### Sprint Manifest Required Fields

Each sprint manifest must record at least:

- `id`
- `title`
- `status`
- `goal`
- `opened_at`
- `updated_at`
- `authority_refs`
- `scope`
- `excluded_boundaries`
- `expected_change_classes`
- `included_tickets` or `iterations`
- `closure_trigger`
- `closure_law`
- `proof_surface`
- `deferred_compliance`
- `non_closure_conditions`
- `paydown_policy`

`authority_refs` names the upstream Goals, Intent, Product, Requirement,
Design, or other governing surfaces the sprint operates under.

`excluded_boundaries` names what the sprint is not allowed to change. Typical
exclusions include product truth, data contracts, runtime semantics,
governance/closure law, public carrier shape, and release criteria.

`deferred_compliance` names any local proof, review, accessibility, screenshot,
walkthrough, test, design wording, or trace cleanup intentionally deferred until
sprint close.

`paydown_policy` states how deferred debt becomes accepted, ticketed, repriced,
or removed during close review.

### Sprint Status

Minimum sprint status model:

- `active`
- `closing`
- `closed`
- `superseded`

The intended meaning is:

- `active`: iteration is admitted inside the sprint boundary
- `closing`: new iteration is frozen while close review and paydown
  classification run
- `closed`: close review finished and all remaining debt is accepted, ticketed,
  repriced, or removed
- `superseded`: the sprint boundary was wrong and a new authority surface,
  sprint, or ticket set replaced it

Projects may add `planned` or `cancelled` if needed, but those states do not
replace close review.

### Sprint Admission

A sprint may admit work only when the manifest makes the boundary reviewable.

Admission requires:

- a bounded scope
- cited authority
- expected change classes
- explicit excluded boundaries
- a closure law
- non-closure conditions
- a paydown policy for deferred compliance

The sprint may batch repeated closure criteria that would otherwise be copied
into every included ticket.

The sprint may not batch away intake triage. Substantive included tickets still
record their lawful `change_class` and `re_entry_point`. Manifest-local
iteration entries may rely on the sprint's declared class only when they remain
inside the sprint scope and excluded boundaries.

### Sprint Compliance Escrow

A sprint may defer local compliance proof only when:

- the manifest names the deferred proof or cleanup class
- the debt is local to the sprint's admitted surface
- expected correction cost is lower than per-change proof cost
- the sprint is short enough that the debt remains reviewable
- the close review must classify and pay down the debt

Deferred compliance is not silent debt. It is escrow held by the sprint.

The following may be eligible for escrow when the governing method allows it:

- screenshots or walkthrough capture
- visual review
- accessibility cleanup
- replay proof for product-meaningful UX interactions
- design wording cleanup
- trace cleanup
- local realization cleanup

The following may not be hidden in escrow:

- new product truth
- new or changed data contracts
- new runtime, governance, closure, provenance, or evidence semantics
- missing constructive carriers
- changed public graph functions or AssetSurface contracts
- law-changing work that needs `goal_reprice`, `intent_reprice`,
  `product_reprice`, `requirement_reprice`, or `design_reframe`

If one of those appears during the sprint, the sprint records the finding and
the work exits the sprint path through a standalone ticket, a repricing action,
or sprint supersession.

### Sprint Close Review

Sprint close begins by moving the manifest to `status: closing`.

While closing:

- new iteration inside that sprint is frozen
- every included ticket or iteration entry is reviewed against the manifest
- accumulated evidence is checked for durability
- changed surfaces are walked against cited authority
- deferred compliance is classified
- paydown tickets are opened where debt must survive past the close review

Each reviewed item is classified as one of:

- `accepted`: compliant under the sprint authority
- `local_paydown`: local debt remains and is captured by a paydown ticket
- `design_reframe`: the work needs design repricing
- `requirement_reprice`: the work needs requirement repricing
- `product_reprice`: the work changes product definition
- `remove`: the work should be backed out or kept out of closure

A sprint may move to `closed` only when every item and every debt entry is
classified and the resulting paydown or repricing work is durable.

Sprint close can accept local paydown debt only when the governing method allows
that debt to survive as explicit follow-up. Sprint close cannot accept hidden
authority drift.
